entries.title: Bandwidth Control Support for the HTTP/2 Protocol
body: Bandwidth Control takes effect for HTTP/2 protocol traffic in addition to the existing protocols already supported.
To enable this feature, contact Zscaler Support.
To learn more, see About Bandwidth Control, Configuring the Bandwidth Control Policy, and Adding Rules to the Bandwidth Control Policy.

entries.title: Enhancements for End User Isolation Experience
body: Enhancements have been made to several features of the end user isolation experience. Depending on your isolation profile settings, you can explore the following features and functionalities in the Zero Trust Mode menu during an isolated session:
- Clipboard: Use clipboard functions (e.g., copy and paste) and view notifications about clipboard restrictions. To learn more, see Using Clipboard in Isolation.
- Translate: Translate the entire web page or selected text from the web page into your preferred language. To learn more, see Understanding Language Translate for Isolation.
- Find: Search text within the web page.
- Troubleshoot: View network latency and export isolation session logs. To learn more, see Accessing Network Latency in Isolation.
See image.
To learn more, see Using the Zero Trust Mode Menu in Native Browser Experience.

entries.title: Advanced SSPM Support for Adobe Acrobat Sign
body: Advanced SSPM supports a new platform, Adobe Acrobat Sign. You can onboard an Adobe Acrobat Sign tenant from the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal.
See image.
To learn more, see Integrating with Adobe Acrobat Sign and Connecting Your Platforms to Advanced SSPM.

entries.title: Advanced SSPM Support for Kintone
body: Advanced SSPM supports a new platform, Kintone. You can onboard a Kintone tenant from the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal.
See image.
To learn more, see Integrating with Kintone and Connecting Your Platforms to Advanced SSPM.

entries.title: Increased Archive Scan Depth with Advanced Sandbox
body: With Advanced Sandbox, you can scan archive files with up to 10 nested archives for threats. To increase the archive scan depth, contact your Zscaler Account team.
To learn more, see About Sandbox.

entries.title: Enterprise Browser for Mobile
body: Enterprise Browser for Zero Trust Browser is available as a native mobile application for iOS, iPadOS, and Android. On a personal or corporate phone or tablet, the Enterprise Browser mobile app provides a governed workspace that enforces policy, prevents data loss, and protects users from everyday browser-based threats.
See image.

Distribution of the app depends on whether the device is personal, corporate managed, or enrolled in a bring-your-own-device (BYOD) program. Users can install the app from the App Store or Google Play, or admins can push the app to users via your organization's Mobile Device Management (MDM) or Mobile Application Management (MAM) platform.
To learn more, see Understanding Enterprise Browser for Mobile.

entries.title: Test Domains for DNS Control Policy Validation
body: Zscaler provides a set of standardized, immutable test FQDNs to validate DNS Control policies. These FQDNs maintain persistent categorization, allowing users to verify that DNS Control policies are applied as intended.
To learn more, see DNS Test Domains.

entries.title: Enhancement to Key Length for Custom Certificate
body: On the Intermediate CA Certificates page (Internet Access > Resources > SSL Intermediate Certificate), you can configure the Software Protection Intermediate CA Certificate and Cloud HSM Intermediate CA Certificate with the key sizes RSA 2048 and EC P-256.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Software Protection Intermediate CA Certificate, and Configuring Cloud HSM Intermediate CA Certificate.

You can create an SSL/TLS Inspection policy with RSA 2K and ECDSA certificates under the Intermediate CA Certificate category (Internet Access > Policy > SSL/TLS Inspection > Add Rule > Action > Intermediate CA Certificate).
To learn more, see Configuring SSL Inspection Policy.

entries.title: Configuring Outbound Email DLP Policy Rules to Match Only Specified Engines
body: The Zscaler Outbound Email Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy supports the Match Only option to specify whether the Zscaler service takes action on sensitive content based on the engines associated with a single rule or on multiple overlapping rules.

When you enable this option, the Zscaler service takes action on message content only when it contains sensitive data that exclusively matches the engines selected for the rule. When you disable this option, the Zscaler service takes action on message content based on the engines associated with the rule, but it can also consider additional content that matches engines in other rules so that more or less restrictive policies can take effect.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Outbound Email Policy Rules and DLP Policy Configuration Example: Match Only.

entries.title: Software Upgrade for Viewing Files in Isolation
body: The software used to render and view files in isolation was upgraded to Apryse WebViewer 12.1.1.
To learn more, see Transferring and Viewing Files in Isolation.

entries.title: Azure Cloud Storage Destinations for Traffic Capture for NDR
body: With Zscaler Traffic Capture for Network Detection and Response (NDR), you can configure Microsoft Azure cloud storage destinations for the Traffic Capture policy.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Settings for the Traffic Capture Policy.

entries.title: Traffic Capture Settings Endpoints
body: You can create, update, and retrieve Traffic Capture settings for an organization, and validate connectivity to a cloud storage provider before creating or updating your organization's Traffic Capture settings using the following endpoints:
- GET /pcapSettings
- POST /pcapSettings
- PUT /pcapSettings/{id}
- POST /pcapSettings/testConnection
To learn more about each endpoint, see the API Reference and API Rate Limit Summary.

entries.title: Increased File Size Support for Advanced Detections
body: With the Advanced Detections package for Advanced Sandbox, you can analyze EXE and DLL files with sizes up to 200 MB.
To learn more, see About Sandbox.

entries.title: Granular Action for Cloud Applications
body: You can granularly control login access for specific cloud applications. The Login granular action has been added to the following Cloud App Control policy rules:
- AI & ML Applications: Controls ChatGPT login for either all domains or specific domains (using domain profiles).
- Collaboration and Online Meetings: Controls login access for:
- Slack: Either all domains or specific domains (using domain profiles).
- Nulab: All domains.
- System & Development: Controls GitHub login for all domains.
- File Sharing: Controls Box login for all domains.
- IT Services: Controls logins for either all domains or specific domains (using domain profiles) for:
- Gmail, Google Drive, Google Gemini, and YouTube (via Google Login Services)
- Yahoo Mail (via Yahoo Login Services)
- Social Networking: Controls logins for all domains for X (formerly Twitter) and Facebook.
- Productivity and CRM Tools: Controls Zendesk login for all domains.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding Rules to the Cloud App Control Policy.

entries.title: Outbound Email DLP Support for Scanning Email Headers
body: Zscaler Outbound Email Data Loss Prevention (DLP) supports scanning email headers to look for sensitive data. As part of your outbound email DLP policy rules, you can specify Email Headers as one of the Content Locations scanned by the Zscaler service.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Outbound Email Policy Rules.

entries.title: SaaS Authenticated Username and Email Recipients Information in Logs
body: Two new columns, SaaS Authenticated Username and Email Recipients, are available on the Web Insights Logs page.
See image.
To learn more, see Web Insights Logs: Columns.

entries.title: Support for Docusign in Tenant Profile
body: The Tenant Profiles feature is extended to the Docusign application. This allows you to provide access to specific application IDs for Docusign.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding Tenant Profiles.
# Docusign Application Support to Tenancy Restriction Profile APIs
A new enum, DOCUSIGN, is added to the appType field of the TenancyRestrictionProfile model referenced by the GET /tenancyRestrictionProfile and GET /tenancyRestrictionProfile/{profileId} APIs.
To learn more, go to TenancyRestrictionProfile model from Cloud App Control Policy.

entries.title: Support for Israel National ID Endpoint DLP Dictionary
body: The Israel National Identification Number predefined Data Loss Prevention (DLP) dictionary is now supported for use in Endpoint DLP policy rules.
To learn more, see Understanding Predefined DLP Dictionaries.

entries.title: Support for New Predefined DLP Dictionaries
body: The following predefined Data Loss Prevention (DLP) dictionaries are now supported for use in Endpoint DLP policy rules:
- National Identification Number (Turkey)
- Permanent Account Number (India)
- United Kingdom Tax Identification Number
To learn more, see Understanding Predefined DLP Dictionaries.

entries.title: Transaction Message in SaaS Insights Logs
body: A new filter and column, Transaction Message, is available on the SaaS Insights Logs page for File application category to view and filter failed SaaS application transactions based on error type.
See image.
To learn more, see About SaaS Security Insights Logs.

entries.title: Enhancement to Filters in 3rd-Party App Governance and Advanced SSPM
body: The Notes filter is added to the Posture and Apps pages. You can use this filter option to filter the controls and apps displayed on these pages based on whether they have notes added to them.
See image.
To learn more, see About Posture and About the App Inventory.

entries.title: Endpoint DLP 26.08 Enhancements and Fixes
body: - Expanded Device Control Support for Portable Devices, CD/DVD, and Floppy Disks
- Device Control now supports portable devices such as smartphones and cameras, CD/DVD, and floppy disk channels.
- Floppy disk is supported on Windows only.
- This release also introduces support for selecting multiple devices and additional resources for managing device criteria.
- To learn more, see About Device Control, Managing a Portable Device Rule, Managing a CD/DVD Rule, Managing a Floppy Disk Rule, and About Resources.
- DLP Intent Visibility Into Suspicious User Behavior
- Data Loss Prevention (DLP) Intent provides visibility into potential insider risk by identifying user behaviors that might indicate suspicious activity, including:
- Abnormal behavior
- Evasive actions
- Data manipulation activities
- To learn more, see About Indicators of Intent and Managing an Intent Rule.
- Inbound Visibility for Sensitive Files Entering Endpoints
- Gain visibility into sensitive files ingress to the endpoint when files containing one or more DLP engines introduced through:
- Files downloaded from the web
- Files copied locally from network shares
- Files copied from removable storage
- Refreshed User Investigation Overview
- User Investigation now shows an enhanced experience with a refreshed interface and a consolidated view of users, devices, and activities in one place.
- To learn more, see Analyzing Endpoint DLP Scan for a User: Overview, Analyzing Endpoint DLP Scan for a User: Data at Rest, and Analyzing Endpoint DLP Scan for a User: Timeline.
- CSV Export for Application Inventory
- The Application Inventory page supports exporting data to CSV for easier analysis and reporting.
- To learn more, see About the Application Investigation Inventory.
- DLP Operational Visibility for macOS Full Disk Access Gaps
- DLP Operational now shows macOS devices that do not have Full Disk Access permission enabled, helping administrators identify and address coverage gaps.
- To learn more, see About DLP Operational.
- IDM Enhancements for DLP Engine Selection and Full-Folder Indexing
- This release includes the following IDM improvements:
- During IDM template creation, the full list of DLP engines is now available for selection.
- At the endpoint, you can now index all files within a folder instead of being limited to up to 20 files.
- To learn more, see Configuring Sensitive Information Settings.
- Configuration Options for OCR, Exclusions, Scan Throttling, and Reporting
- The following configuration options are added to the Configuration page:
- OCR now supports PDFs and runs in real-time for all channels except Application File Access.
- Exclude files and folders from continuous classification and application scans.
- Pause scans based on an administrator-defined CPU threshold.
- Exclude trusted applications from Endpoint DLP inspection.
- Limit reporting to only matched DLP dictionaries and DLP engines based on triggered policies.
- Exclude console applications from both Printing and Clipboard channels on Windows.
- To learn more, see Configuring Endpoint Data Scan, Endpoint Settings, and Channels.

entries.title: Increased Sublocations Limit for a Location
body: You can add up to 16K sublocations per location.
To learn more, see Configuring Sublocations and Ranges and Limitations.

entries.title: Support for New SSPM Controls for Google Workspace
body: The number of SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) controls for Google Workspace has been increased. There are 53 new cloud identity controls and 7 new mobile device controls that are supported for Google Workspace.
You must add additional OAuth scopes for the new controls.
To learn more, see Authorizing a Custom Zscaler Connector for Google Applications.

entries.title: Support for Personal Email Detection in Outbound Email DLP Policy
body: The Zscaler service supports configuring your Outbound Email Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy rules to include detection of personal email addresses. When you select this option, the rule detects when end users attempt to send sensitive data to their personal email address by matching the user’s organizational name with recipient names on external email domains (e.g., Gmail or Yahoo). This option ensures that the rule is enforced only when the recipient is the sender’s personal email address.
See image.
A filter and column, Personal Email, is added to the Email DLP Insights Logs page to display the user’s personal email address when the email is sent to the user's personal email address.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Outbound Email Policy Rules, Email DLP Insights Logs: Filters, and Email DLP Insights Logs: Columns.

entries.title: Support for Selective Monitoring for Slack Workspaces
body: You can choose to monitor specific workspaces within your Slack enterprise account for DLP and Malware scanning using a custom connector. While onboarding your Slack tenant, authorize Zscaler service via a custom connector with necessary permissions.
See image.
Additionally, on the Scan Configuration page, you can see a new option, Chat Bots. You can choose to either include or exclude chatbots from the scan.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding SaaS Application Tenants, Authorizing a Custom Zscaler Connector for Slack, About SaaS Security Scan Configuration, and Configuring SaaS Security Scan Schedules.

entries.title: Unified Role-Based Access Control for Internet & SaaS
body: Internet & SaaS (ZIA) supports Unified Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). Administrators can now view, create, and manage Internet & SaaS roles centrally on the Role Management page (Administration > Role Management > Role Management).
The existing Internet & SaaS Role Management page is deprecated if you use Unified RBAC.
To access Unified RBAC, contact your Zscaler Account team.
To learn more, see About Role Management.

entries.title: DLP and EDM Support for NFKC Normalization
body: To enable this feature for your organization, contact Zscaler Support.

As part of Zscaler Data Loss Prevention (DLP) phrase matching and Exact Data Match (EDM) indexing, the Zscaler service supports Normalization Form Compatibility Composition (NFKC). During DLP processing and EDM indexing, the Zscaler service converts all recognized unicode full-width characters into half-width characters, as in the following examples:
| Original Full-Width Characters | Converted Half-Width Characters |
| テラシマハルカ | ﾃﾗｼﾏﾊﾙｶ |
| ＡＢＣＤＥ | ABCDE |
| ＣＤＥＦ ＡＢＣ ３４５ | CDEF ABC 345 |
To learn more, see About Data Loss Prevention and About Exact Data Match.

entries.title: Enhancement to Browser Control Policy
body: You can create policies, configure browser control, and configure HTTP header control for the Brave browser. As part of this update, the Brave browser is supported in the following locations:
- Cloud App Control Policy: In the User Agent criterion of the Add Rule page.
- See image.
- SSL/TLS Inspection Policy: In the User Agent criterion of the Add Rule page.
- See image.
- URL Filtering Policy: In the User Agent criterion of the Add Rule page.
- See image.
- Browser Control: In the Browser Blocking section.
- See image.
- HTTP Header Control: In the Browser field of the User Agent HTTP header.
- See image.

entries.title: Security Fixes
body: The Internet & SaaS (ZIA) File Type Control evaluation rule no longer allows a potential evasion of File Type Control policies (CVE-2026-25684).

entries.title: Support for AI Transcript and Summary for a Zoom Tenant
body: You can onboard a Zoom tenant enabled with the Data at Rest Scanning Data Loss Prevention (DLP) and Malware functionality to scan two additional content types: AI transcript and AI meeting summary.
You must enable AI Companion for your Zoom account to generate transcripts and summaries.

To enable the AI Transcripts and Summaries capability for an existing tenant, you must add additional scopes, subscribe to additional transcript and summary webhook events, and reauthorize the tenant.
To learn more, see Adding SaaS Application Tenants.

entries.title: Support for User Group Filter in Logs
body: You can filter logs for specific user groups. As part of the update, the following changes are available in the Zscaler Admin Console:
- The User Group filter is added to the following Insights Logs pages:
- Web Insights Logs
- Firewall Insights Logs
- DNS Insights Logs
- SaaS Security Insights Logs
- Endpoint DLP Insights Logs
- Email DLP Insights Logs
- See image.
- The User Group filter is available when configuring Dashboard and Interactive Report widgets.
- See image.
- The following data types are available under the Web data class in the Interactive Reports:
- URL Filtering Policy
- Cloud App Control Policy
- To learn more, see Web Data Types and Filters, Mobile Data Types and Filters, Firewall Data Types and Filters, and DNS Data Types and Filters.

entries.title: Update to Add SaaS Application Tenant Page
body: When onboarding a Software as a Service (SaaS) application tenant, you can no longer select the App Governance functionality. If you select the SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) Scan checkbox for applications that support App Governance, you can scan both SSPM security checks and SSPM 3rd-party add-ons.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding SaaS Application Tenants.

entries.title: Cloud App Control Policy: Upload Action for Google Gemini
body: The Cloud App Control policy supports granular upload action for the Google Gemini application. This allows you to control the upload action for Google Gemini or instances of it. As part of this change, the Uploading granular action is added to the Allow application access in the Add/Edit AI & ML Rule window.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding an AI & ML Applications Rule for Cloud App Control.

entries.title: Support for New Match Type on Custom DLP Dictionaries
body: Custom Data Loss Prevention (DLP) dictionaries support near and not near proximity. This functionality helps you define how close (in bytes) phrases from phrase groups must be for a dictionary to detect and count them as a match.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding Custom DLP Dictionaries.

entries.title: Added Support for Enhanced Dictionaries and Sub-Dictionaries
body: The Zscaler service supports the following predefined Data Loss Prevention (DLP) dictionaries:
- Enhanced Credentials and Secrets
- Enhanced International Bank Account Number (IBAN)
- Enhanced Passport Number (Asia)
- Enhanced Passport Number (European Union)
The parent dictionaries contain predefined sub-dictionaries, and each sub-dictionary can be individually referenced in your DLP engines.

On the DLP Dictionaries & Engines page (Policies > Data Protection > Common Resources > DLP Dictionaries & Engines), you can expand each dictionary's section to see its sub-dictionary. You can configure each of the individual sub-dictionaries to set the Confidence Score Threshold, Proximity Length, and any Custom High Confidence Phrases.
See image.

- The Enhanced dictionaries for Credentials and Secrets, Driver License (US), International Bank Account Number, Passport Number (Asia), and Passport Number (European Union) are not supported for Endpoint DLP.

- The legacy dictionaries for Credentials and Secrets, Driver License (US), International Bank Account Number, Passport Number (Asia), and Passport Number (European Union) have been replaced, but not deprecated, by the Enhanced Credentials and Secrets, Enhanced Driver License (US), Enhanced International Bank Account Number, Enhanced Passport Number (Asia), and Enhanced Passport Number (European Union) predefined dictionaries.
To learn more, see Understanding Predefined DLP Dictionaries.

entries.title: Cloning of Predefined DLP Sub-Dictionaries
body: You can clone predefined Data Loss Prevention (DLP) sub-dictionaries. Predefined DLP sub-dictionaries are hierarchical child dictionaries associated with predefined DLP dictionaries. Cloning a predefined DLP sub-dictionary creates a separate copy that you can customize with different confidence score thresholds and other dictionary-specific parameters without modifying the original sub-dictionary.
See image.
To learn more, see Cloning Predefined DLP Dictionaries.

entries.title: DLP Support for Credit Card Image Dictionary
body: DLP now supports the Credit Card Image predefined dictionary, which detects images of credit cards in supported file types such as JPEG and PNG.
See image.
To learn more, see Understanding Predefined DLP Dictionaries.

entries.title: New File Type Support for Outbound Email DLP Policy
body: The Outbound Email Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy now supports Microsoft TNEF files. The file type is available when creating Outbound Email DLP policies without content inspection:
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Outbound Email Policy Rules.

entries.title: Secure Email Gateway Support in Outbound Email DLP Policies
body: You can use Zscaler Outbound Email Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies with your secure email gateway (SEG) to prevent the exfiltration of sensitive data by enforcing policy rules on email content sent to external domains, including content in subject lines, body text, and attachments. As part of your larger DLP strategy, Zscaler Outbound Email DLP for SEGs lets you use the same DLP policy tools that you already use across other channels (i.e., Inline Web DLP, Endpoint DLP, and SaaS Security Data at Rest Scanning DLP), eliminating the need for different DLP point solutions and the operational overhead involved in maintaining those solutions. Additionally, you can monitor outbound email activity with dashboards, reports, and NSS feeds. This enhancement supplements existing Outbound Email DLP support for Microsoft Exchange and Gmail.
Because of recent enhancements to next-hop validation that enforce stricter security checks during SMTP connections, the Zscaler service:
- Strictly enforces SSL/TLS for secure SMTP connections.
- Performs server certificate validation that requires the presented certificate to be valid and trusted.
- Does not allow self-signed, expired, or otherwise invalid certificates.
As you set up Email tenants in the Zscaler Admin Console (Policies > Data Protection > Policy > Email Tenants), you have the option to select an SEG tenant.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding Email Tenants and Configuring SEGs for Zscaler Outbound Email DLP.

entries.title: Support for Claude in Tenant Profile
body: The Tenant Profiles feature is extended to the Claude application. This allows you to provide access to specific workspace IDs for Claude.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding Tenant Profiles.
# Claude Application Support to Tenancy Restriction Profile APIs

A new enum, CLAUDE_AI, is added to the appType query parameter in the GET /tenancyRestrictionProfile/app-item-count/{appType}/{itemType} endpoint. CLAUDE_AI is also added to the appType field of the TenancyRestrictionProfile model referenced by the tenancy restriction profile APIs.
To learn more, go to TenancyRestrictionProfile model and GET /tenancyRestrictionProfile/app-item-count/{appType}/{itemType} from Cloud App Control Policy.

entries.title: Configure DLP Cloud-to-Cloud Incident Forwarding for Microsoft Azure with Private Key
body: You can now authenticate Microsoft Azure using a private key when configuring DLP Cloud-to-Cloud Incident Forwarding. Private key authentication uses an Azure app registration certificate to authenticate without storing a client secret.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring DLP Cloud-to-Cloud Incident Forwarding for Microsoft Azure.

entries.title: Enhancements to Cloud-to-Cloud DLP Incident Receiver Endpoints
body: A new query parameter excludeDisabledC2CForwarding is available for the GET /cloudToCloudIR, GET /cloudToCloudIR/lite, and GET /cloudToCloudIR/count APIs. Also, a new field, featuresSupported is added to the C2CIncidentReceiver referenced by the Cloud-to-Cloud DLP Incident Receiver APIs, providing the list of features supported by the Cloud-to-Cloud DLP Incident Receiver endpoints.
To learn more, go to /cloudToCloudIR from Data Loss Prevention.

entries.title: Support for External Link Expiration in Google Drive
body: You can set a periodic or custom expiration period for your Google Drive links (internal or external). Access to the files is automatically revoked after the expiration period.
In the Edit DLP rule window, four new actions with expiration have been added:
- Remove Collaborators After Expiry
- Remove External Sharing Links After Expiry
- Remove Internal Sharing Links After Expiry
- Remove Sharing After Expiry
See image.
Additionally, you can also set manual expiration for Google Drive under Remediation Actions on the SaaS Assets with Incidents page.
To learn more, see:
- Configuring the Data at Rest Scanning DLP Policy with Content Inspection
- Configuring the Data at Rest Scanning DLP Policy without Content Inspection
- Understanding SaaS Security API Supported Capabilities Draft
- Understanding the Assets Report: Assets with Incidents
# Enhancements to the SaaS Security Data at Rest Scanning Data Loss Prevention (DLP) APIs

Enum values OFLCASB_DLP_REMOVE_COLLABORATORS_EXPIRY, OFLCASB_DLP_REMOVE_SHARING_EXPIRY, OFLCASB_DLP_REMOVE_INTERNAL_LINK_SHARE_EXPIRY, and OFLCASB_DLP_REMOVE_EXTERNAL_LINK_SHARE_EXPIRY are added to the action field in the CASBDlpRule model referenced by the /casbDlpRules APIs. For a Google Drive tenant, these enum values allow you to:
- remove collaborators after expiration
- remove sharing after expiration
- remove internal sharing links after expiration
- remove external sharing links after expiration

Additionally, two new fields, fileSharingExpiryTimeType and fileSharingExpiryTime are available in the CASBDlpRule model referenced by the /casbDlpRules APIs. These fields are required to set the file sharing expiration period. To learn more, go to the CASBDlpRule model from SaaS Security API.

entries.title: Enhancement to IDM Profile Endpoints
body: The profileId field in the IdmProfile object used by the /idmprofile APIs provides an enhanced limit to the Indexed Document Match (IDM) profile index tool template, increasing from 64 to 512.

entries.title: New Network Applications in Firewall Control
body: The Zscaler service extends support to identify the following new network applications:
- WARP under the Tunneled Traffic category
- DOQ, DOH3, STOMP, and AMQP under the Network Service category
You can view these apps on the Network Applications page and configure them in Firewall Filtering rules to identify and manage associated traffic.
To learn more, see About Network Applications.

entries.title: Support for Go to File Action for Salesforce
body: The Go to File action enables you to easily navigate to the location of a violated file in Salesforce.
See image.
To learn more, see Understanding the Assets Report: Assets with Incidents.

entries.title: Support for Jira Application Label in SaaS Security Data at Rest Scanning DLP Policies
body: The SaaS Security Data at Rest Scanning DLP Policies support a new action that allows you to apply Jira Application Labels when creating SaaS Security Data at Rest Scanning DLP Policy rules in the Zscaler Admin Console by going to Policies > Data Protection > Policy > Out-of-Band CASB and selecting the Data Loss Prevention tab. Tenants support the Apply Jira Classification Label Action for DLP rules with the ITSM Application.

To learn more, see Configuring the Data at Rest Scanning DLP Policy with Content Inspection Configuring the Data at Rest Scanning DLP Policy without Content Inspection, and Understanding SaaS Security Supported Capabilities.

entries.title: WebSocket Inspection Enhancements
body: Zscaler inspects bidirectional WebSocket traffic across applications, allowing you to extend security and data protection controls to these communications. This inspection applies to WebSocket traffic carrying supported content. Advanced inspection scenarios, including support for other payload types, might require application-specific support (e.g., Microsoft Copilot or Grammarly).

To learn more, see Configuring the URL Filtering Policy, Adding Rules to the Bandwidth Control Policy, Web Insights Logs: Filters, Mobile Insights Logs: Filters, and Configuring the Firewall Filtering Policy.

entries.title: Enhancements for End User Isolation Experience for Clipboard Functions
body: If an admin configures restrictions to clipboard actions for a user's profile and the user attempts those actions, the user sees a notification appear in the Zero Trust Mode menu. If clicked, the Clipboard sidebar opens and shows the details of the notification for the restriction attempt.
See image.
To learn more, see Using the Zero Trust Mode Menu in Native Browser Experience.

entries.title: Enhancements for End User Isolation Experience for File Transfers
body: The following updates have been made to the end user isolation experience for Zero Trust Browser:

- Download Completion: When a user downloads a file while in isolation, a temporary notification appears to confirm when the file has completed downloading. The user can click the View button from the notification to see the file name and location in the Protected Storage. Additionally, they can click the Protected Storage icon from the Zero Trust Mode menu to open the Protected Storage section and view all file transfer notifications.
- See image.

- Upload Options: A user can upload a file in multiple different ways while in isolation, such as using the Upload File button in the Protected Storage and uploading files from their local machine to a website.
- See image.
To learn more, see Using the Zero Trust Mode Menu in Native Browser Experience and Transferring and Viewing Files in Isolation.

entries.title: Enhancements for End User Isolation Experience Session Indicator & Menu
body: The Zero Trust Mode icon that indicates a live isolation session for Zero Trust Browser hides an expandable menu for the user to access different functions:
- The Protected Storage icon allows users to view all file transfers for the isolation session.
- The Clipboard icon allows users to view notifications about clipboard functions and restrictions.
- The Print icon allows users to view options and information for printing settings.
- The Troubleshoot icon allows users to start a debug session, view network latency, access ip.zscaler.com, or export isolation session logs.
- The Information icon allows users to view the settings configured by admins for an isolation profile. This includes user restrictions and disabled tools.
Clicking the checkmark Zero Trust Mode icon at the bottom of the menu collapses the options back under the floating icon.
See image.
To learn more, see Using the Zero Trust Mode Menu in Native Browser Experience.

entries.title: Canada Region Added to Isolation Profiles in Internet & SaaS
body: Canada has been added as an isolation region in Zero Trust Browser. You can select the region when configuring isolation profiles for Internet & SaaS (ZIA).
See image.
To learn more, see Creating Isolation Profiles for Internet & SaaS.

entries.title: New Search Filters for Firewall Filtering Policy Rules
body: The following update is applicable only to tenants approved for an increased rule limit of up to 4,000 Firewall Filtering rules, based on qualified use cases.
The Firewall Filtering Policy page includes the following new search filters:
- Rule Status
- Network Application Groups
- Application Service Groups
- Source Country
- Destination Country
- Source IPv6 Groups
- Destination IPv6 Groups

Rule Status, Source Country, and Destination Country filters require you to select from predefined values to filter the associated rules, whereas the remaining new filters support searching by entity names (e.g., Network Application Groups requires manually entering group names to filter the associated rules). Source IPv6 Groups and Destination IPv6 Groups filters appear only when IPv6 configuration is enabled for your organization.
See image.
To learn more, About Firewall Filtering.

entries.title: Support for Select All and Hide Deleted for Log Filtering
body: You can select all and hide deleted users, departments, and locations when filtering Insights Logs. As part of the enhancement, the following updates are available in the Zscaler Admin Console:
# Insights Logs
The Select All and Hide Deleted options are added to the Users, Departments, and Locations filter in the following Insights Logs pages:
- Web Insights Logs
- Firewall Insights Logs
- DNS Insights Logs
- Tunnel Insights Logs
- SaaS Security Insights Logs
- Endpoint DLP Insights Logs
- Email DLP Insights Logs
See image.
# Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS)
The Select All and Hide Deleted options are added to the Users, Departments, and Locations filters in TCP NSS, MCAS NSS, HTTP NSS, and Cloud NSS feeds for the following log types, as applicable:
- Web
- Firewall
- DNS
- Tunnel
- SaaS Security
- Endpoint DLP
- Email DLP
See image.

entries.title: Virtual Service Edges Supported for Nutanix
body: Virtual Service Edge configuration is supported on the Nutanix platform. You can download the Nutanix VM image on the Virtual Service Edges page.
To learn more, see Configuring Virtual Service Edges for Internet & SaaS: Nutanix.

entries.title: New Cloud Applications
body: New cloud applications are added to the cloud application categories. You can download the list of newly added cloud applications to the respective categories: Download
The risk index and risk attribute values for these new applications are visible only after they are available on all the clouds. Refer to the trust post for details.

entries.title: NSS Support for 3rd-Party App Governance and Posture Management Logs
body: Logs for Zscaler 3rd-Party App Governance and Posture Management are supported by Zscaler's Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS). You can configure NSS and Cloud NSS feeds for both log types to stream their respective data to your security information and event management (SIEM) system, providing a unified view of your organization’s security posture for effective threat management.
Access to these log types requires a subscription to Advanced SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM). To subscribe to Advanced SSPM, contact your Zscaler Account team.
See image.
When creating a policy in 3rd-Party App Governance, you can select the Zscaler Nanolog Streaming Service option to receive alerts for the policy through NSS every time the policy is triggered.
See image.
To learn more, see:
- Adding NSS Feeds for 3rd-Party App Governance Logs
- Adding Cloud NSS Feeds for 3rd-Party App Governance Logs
- NSS Feed Output Format: 3rd-Party App Governance Logs
- Adding NSS Feeds for Posture Management Logs
- Adding Cloud NSS Feeds for Posture Management Logs
- NSS Feed Output Format: Posture Management Logs
- 3rd-Party App Governance Policies
# Enhancement to Cloud Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) API
Two new enum values, POSTURE_CONTROL and APP_GOVERNANCE are added to the nssLogType field in the ZmanageNssFeed model referenced by the /nssFeeds APIs
To learn more, go to the ZmanageNssFeed model from Cloud Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS).

entries.title: Updates to Cloud Applications
body: As part of a continuous review, Zscaler has updated cloud applications across various cloud application categories. To obtain the list of cloud applications that have been updated, download the list: Download
Cloud applications are updated in phases. Refer to the trust post for details.

entries.title: Enterprise Browser for Zero Trust Browser
body: Enterprise Browser for Zero Trust Browser is a dedicated, hardened Chromium browser that protects users from everyday browser-based threats. Users can access private applications for their organization while utilizing browser protection for daily operations such as file transfer, data sharing, and cloud service authentication.
To learn more, see Understanding Enterprise Browser.

entries.title: Additional Support for Microsoft 365 Apps in Advanced SSPM
body: Advanced SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) supports new posture controls as part of the Microsoft 365 connector for the following apps:
- Microsoft Power Apps
- Microsoft Power BI
- Microsoft Purview
- Microsoft Viva Engage
Existing tenants must grant additional permissions and reauthenticate the connector for these additional posture controls.
Select the SSPM Scan checkbox when onboarding a Microsoft 365 tenant to enable the Advanced SSPM scan capability for the specific tenant.
See image.
The SSPM Scan checkbox is enabled only when you have Advanced SSPM enabled for your tenant.
To learn more, see What Is Advanced Posture Management?, Adding SaaS Application Tenants, and Authorizing a Custom Zscaler Connector for Microsoft Applications.

entries.title: Block Domain Fronting Enhancement
body: In Advanced Settings (Policies > Common Configuration > Advanced > Advanced Settings > Domain Fronting), there are two new options available under Block Domain Fronting:
- URL Category Exemptions for Block Domain Fronting: Select the URL categories you want to exempt from domain fronting.
- Exempted Cloud Applications for Block Domain Fronting: Select the cloud app categories or cloud apps you want to exempt from domain fronting.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Advanced Settings.

entries.title: Enhanced Web Logs: Added Support for DLP Policy Actions and Justification Messages
body: You can filter and view logs for DLP policy actions and DLP confirmation messages. As part of the update, the following changes are available in the Zscaler Admin Console:
# Insights Logs
Filters and columns, DLP Policy Action and DLP Confirmation Message, are added to Web Insights Logs and Endpoint DLP Insights Logs.
See image.
To learn more, see Web Insights Logs: Columns, Web Insights Logs: Filters, Endpoint DLP Insights Logs: Columns, and Endpoint DLP Insights Logs: Filters.
# NSS Feeds

The fields %s{dlp_policy_action} and %s{dlp_confirm_justification_msg} can be added to the Feed Output Format when configuring an NSS or Cloud NSS feed for web logs. Additionally, the field %s{dlp_confirm_justification_msg} is available for NSS and Cloud NSS feeds for Endpoint DLP logs.
To learn more, see NSS Feed Output Format: Web Logs and NSS Feed Output Format: Endpoint DLP Logs.

entries.title: New Labels and Values in SaaS Security Report
body: Instead of classifying all new applications as Unsanctioned, you can use new Application Status labels Unclassified and Under Review, to classify applications more appropriately. The label Unclassified means the applications haven't been evaluated for risks yet, and Under Review means they are undergoing due diligence.
See image.

Moreover, the SaaS Security Report for each cloud application now displays detailed information about security attributes including their certificate validity, WAF name, CVE ID, breach URL, and so on. More information appears in brackets next to the Yes and No signals.
See image.
To learn more, see About the SaaS Security Report and About the Application Information.

entries.title: Enhancement to Application Service Groups
body: The Application Services page has been enhanced to allow you to define your own application service groups. This page contains the following enhancements:
- You can add custom application service groups.
- The Definition column is added.
- You can view, edit, and filter the application service groups under a new column.
The Custom Application Service Group is available if Advanced Firewall is enabled for your organization.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Application Service Groups and About Application Service Groups.
# Update to Forwarding Policy, IPS Control Policy, and Firewall Filtering Policy
The Forwarding policy, IPS Control policy, and Firewall Filtering policy allow you to select predefined (AU) and custom (CU) application service groups while configuring these policies.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Forwarding Policy, Configuring IPS Control Policy, and Configuring the Firewall Filtering Policy.
# Update to Cloud Service API

The cloud service API includes the following new endpoints to create, update, and delete custom application service groups, and retrieve configurations for all custom application service groups (predefined and custom):
- GET /apps-services
- POST /apps-services
- GET /apps-services/{appServiceId}
- PUT /apps-services/{appServiceId}
- DELETE /apps-services/{appServiceId}
To learn more, see the API Reference.

entries.title: Support for Snowflake as an API-Based Platform in Advanced SSPM
body: Advanced SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) supports Snowflake as an API-based platform to provide visibility into posture misconfigurations. You can configure Advanced SSPM for Snowflake tenants. Select the SSPM Scan checkbox when onboarding a tenant to enable the Advanced SSPM scan capability for the specific tenant.

The SSPM Scan checkbox is enabled only when you have Advanced SSPM enabled for your tenant.
To learn more, see What Is Advanced Posture Management? and Adding SaaS Application Tenants.

entries.status: Feature Available: Endpoint DLP 26.02.4.2 for Windows

entries.title: Enhancement to Browser EUN Template

entries.title: Advanced SSPM Support for Databricks

See image.

entries.title: Advanced SSPM Support for OpenAI

entries.title: Expanded SSPM Controls for Box

entries.title: Ability to Select Channels for DLP Engines

This functionality is available when you create, edit, or clone a DLP engine on the DLP Engines page (Policies > Data Protection > Common Resources > DLP Dictionaries & Engines > DLP Engines):

To learn more, see Editing Predefined DLP Engines, Adding Custom DLP Engines, and Cloning DLP Engines.

entries.title: New Domain Profile Endpoints in Cloud Service API
body: The cloud service API includes the following new endpoints to add, update, and delete domain profiles and to retrieve information about domain profiles:
- GET /domainProfiles
- POST /domainProfiles
- GET /domainProfiles/{id}
- PUT /domainProfiles/{id}

The Postman Collection is also updated to include new and updated resources. To learn more, see Configuring the Postman REST API Client.

entries.title: Endpoint Context Limited Availability
body: To enable Endpoint Context for your organization, contact Zscaler Support.

Zscaler Endpoint Context extends the Zero Trust Exchange (ZTE) to provide unified cloud-to-endpoint visibility, detection, and dynamic risk-based policy enforcement. This functionality integrates real-time endpoint application data with industry-leading cloud intelligence to help your Security Operations Center (SOC) teams defend your organization from modern, sophisticated, AI-accelerated attacks that often bypass traditional siloed security tools.

Endpoint Context takes advantage of extensive data available from Zscaler Client Connector to provide an inventory of commonly abused applications that reside on each endpoint, both actively running and at rest, and enumerates a rich data set related to each application, including application name, publisher, total instances of an application, install path, etc.

The Application Investigation page (Policies > Cybersecurity > Endpoint Context > Application Investigation) provides a dashboard with useful information about the applications installed on endpoints across your organization. From the Application Investigation page, you can see the Overview page (Policies > Cybersecurity > Endpoint Context > Application Investigation > Overview), which contains useful tables and charts that categorize information about all applications:
See image.

On the Inventory page (Policies > Cybersecurity > Endpoint Context > Application Investigation > Inventory), you can use various criteria (e.g., OS, certificate status, threat type, vulnerabilities) to review the application information most important to your SOC teams:
See image.
You can click any of the applications in the list to drill down to more granular detail:
See image.

Additionally, when you license Endpoint Context for your organization, you have the ability to specify application details for both Windows and macOS endpoints on the DLP & Endpoint Resources page (Policies > Data Protection > Endpoint DLP Resources > Applications):
See image.
You can also add Endpoint Application Tags so that you can group applications by category or theme (e.g., browsers or compression utilities):
See image.

If you have also licensed Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) for your organization, any resource groups that you have already configured are automatically converted to resource tag groups. All policies that previously used resource groups are automatically updated to use the converted resource tag groups.

With applications configured, you can apply your custom application configurations, or use the default configurations provided by the Zscaler service, to various policies in the Zscaler Admin Console (e.g., Advanced Firewall, DNS Control, SSL/TLS Inspection):
See image.
# Update to Cloud Service API

The cloud service API includes new endpoints to create and manage endpoint application resources and updates to existing policy APIs to configure endpoint application-based conditions in policy rules.
- Endpoint Application Resources

- Using the following API endpoints, you can create, update, and delete custom endpoint applications and update and retrieve information about all endpoint applications, including well-known, discovered, and custom applications. You can also retrieve the count of applications available within a specific category and the list of policy rules associated with a specific application.
- GET /endPointApplications/customApps
- POST /endPointApplications/customApp
- PUT /endPointApplications/customApp/{id}
- DELETE /endPointApplications/customApp/{id}
- GET /endPointApplications/customApps/{id}
- GET /endPointApplications/customApps/lite
- GET /endPointApplications
- GET /endPointApplications/lite
- PUT /endPointApplications/{id}
- GET /endPointApplications/cloudApps
- GET /endPointApplications/policies
- GET /endPointApplications/getCategoriesWithNonEmptyApps
- GET /endPointApplications/count
- GET /endPointApplications/cloudApps/count
- To learn more, see the API Reference and API Rate Limit Summary.
- Endpoint Application Tags

- The following API endpoints allow you to create and manage endpoint application tag groups. You can create, update, and delete endpoint application tags and retrieve information about the application tags. You can also manage endpoint applications associated with a tag and retrieve the list of policy rules associated with a tag.
- GET /endPointApplicationGroups
- POST /endPointApplicationGroups
- GET /endPointApplicationGroups/{id}
- PUT /endPointApplicationGroups/{groupId}
- DELETE /endPointApplicationGroups/{id}
- PUT /endPointApplicationGroups/resources/{groupId}
- GET /endPointApplicationGroups/policies
- To learn more, see the API Reference and API Rate Limit Summary.
- Policy Rules

- The SSLInspectionRule, FirewallFilteringRule, and FirewallDnsRule models include the following attributes to configure policy rule conditions based on endpoint applications, endpoint application tags, and endpoint application threat levels:
- endPointApplications
- endPointApplicationGroups
- endPointApplicationThreatLevels
- excludeContextShieldEndPoint (supported only in FirewallFilteringRule and FirewallDnsRule models)

entries.title: Logs for JA4 Network Fingerprinting
body: Enhancements to Insights Logs and the Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) provide real-time visibility into the TLS/SSL server communication by capturing JA4 network fingerprints at the connection level and logging them within the Internet & SaaS (ZIA) web logs. The enhancements enable network security teams to monitor, analyze, and respond to encrypted traffic without waiting for sessions to complete.
As part of the update, the following changes are available in the Zscaler Admin Console:
# Web Insights Logs
The following filters and columns are added to Web Insights Logs:
- JA4 Fingerprint
- JA4 Fingerprint A
- JA4 Fingerprint B
- JA4 Fingerprint C
See image.
To learn more, see Web Insights Logs: Columns and Web Insights Logs: Filters.
# NSS Feeds for Web Logs
The field %s{ja4_str} can be added to the Feed Output Format when configuring an NSS or Cloud NSS feed for web logs.
To learn more, see NSS Feed Output Format: Web Logs.

entries.title: Enhancement to the Cloud Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) API
body: Three new fields, appInventoryAppTypes, appInventoryThreatTypes, and appInventoryThreatCategories, are available for the ZmanageNssFeed model in the /nssFeeds APIs. These fields allow users to filter Application Inventory logs based on the application types, threat types, and threat categories.
To learn more, go to ZmanageNssFeed from Cloud Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS).

entries.title: File Type Control Policy Rule Expiration
body: Admins can set an expiration for File Type Control policy rules.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring the File Type Control Policy.

entries.title: Redactive Sensitive Text for Isolation in Internet & SaaS
body: Zero Trust Browser allows admins to enable the redaction of sensitive text data for configured Data Loss Prevention (DLP) engines and dictionaries based on the DLP configuration in an isolation profile.
See image.
To learn more, see Using Redactive Sensitive Text for Isolation and Creating Isolation Profiles for Internet & SaaS.

entries.title: Secure Message Processing Center (SMPC) Instance Endpoints
body: You can update the data center and the Secure Message Processing Center (SMPC) instance details based on a specific data center ID and retrieve the status of all SMPC instances grouped by a data center using the following endpoints:
- GET /smpcInstance
- PUT /smpcInstance/dc

A new Enum value, ZS_BUSINESS_CONTINUITY is available in the permissions field of the AdminRole model used by the /adminRoles APIs. This enum allows administrators to grant permission to update or view the SMPC instance isolation.
To learn more about each endpoint, see the API Reference and API Rate Limit Summary.

entries.title: Support for End User Migration
body: Authentication Service is the global and centralized identity management platform for all the Zscaler products. You can now migrate all the users from your external IdPs to Authentication Service. This streamlines the identity management process and eliminates the need to configure the IdP for each Zscaler product separately, and instead manage all the idenitites within Authentication Service. After the migration, end users can authenticate with Authentication Service and access the assigned Zscaler services.
To learn more, see Migrating End Users to Authentication Service and What Is Authentication Service?

entries.title: Enhancements for Isolation User Experience Loading Page
body: The following updates have been made to the isolation experience for Zero Trust Browser:

- As you enter an isolated session, a static, temporary message appears in the middle of the web page as it loads to confirm you are entering an isolated session. Additionally, an animated green outline appears around the website border as the page loads.
- See image.

- When the page has completely rendered, a temporary notification banner appears in the upper-right corner that displays a customized notification title. You can click the Show More link in the banner to view a message customized by the admin.
- See image.

- A floating checkmark icon also appears when the page has completely rendered, and stays visible after the temporary notification banner disappears. This is a visual indicator that the isolation session is persisting and has not expired.
- See image.
To learn more, see Adding a Banner Theme for the Isolation End User Notification in ZIA.

entries.title: Updates to Devices Endpoints
body: You can retrieve information about devices registered with Zscaler using the following endpoints:
- GET /devices
- GET /devices/{id}
To learn more about each endpoint, see the API Reference and API Rate Limit Summary.

entries.title: Updates to Partner Integrations APIs
body: You can retrieve a list of partners and services integrated with the Zscaler service, a list of configured CrowdStrike endpoints or device IDs, and detailed endpoint or device data based on the IDs using the following integration endpoints:
- GET /integrationPartners
- GET /integrationPartners/crowdStrike/endpoints
- POST /integrationPartners/crowdStrike/endpoints
- GET /integrationPartners/crowdStrike/whitelistedBaseUrls
You can configure the integration of Microsoft Defender for Endpoint APIs with Zscaler and retrieve the MD5 hash of the file required to view the Sandbox Detail Report using the following endpoints:
- POST /integrationPartners/microsoftDefender/endpoints
- GET /integrationPartners/sandbox/report/{md5}
To learn more about each endpoint, see the API Reference and API Rate Limit Summary.

entries.title: Zscaler URL Category Test
body: The Zscaler URL category test provides a set of standardized, immutable test URLs specifically designed for HTTPS URL policy validation testing. These Zscaler-managed sites maintain persistent categorization, allowing administrators to consistently verify that URL Filtering rules and SSL/TLS Inspection policies are being applied as intended.
Because these URLs are immutable, they provide a baseline for confirming HTTPS URLs and SSL/TLS policy actions without the risk of external site changes.
See image.
To learn more, see About URL Categories.

entries.title: Enhancements to Admin Users and Groups Endpoints
body: A new query parameter, adminScopeSupport, is available for the GET /groups and GET /groups/lite endpoints. adminScopeSupport is also added as a field attribute in the Group model referenced by the groups APIs.
To learn more, go to /groups from User Management.

Additionally, a new Enum value, USER_GROUP, is added to the Enum list in the scope field of the AdminScope and AlertDefinition models. This value is available for all the APIs where scope selection is applicable.

entries.title: Sandbox for Private Access Assets
body: Organizations with Advanced Sandbox that use Internet & SaaS (ZIA) to inspect Private Access (ZPA) traffic can sandbox unknown files uploaded to Private Access assets.
To learn more, see About Sandbox.

entries.title: Support for AI/ML Detection Source
body: The Zscaler Admin Console is enhanced with the ability to view the AI/ML detection source for your Internet & SaaS (ZIA) traffic. The following updates are available:
# Web Insights Logs
The AI/ML Detection Source filter and column are added to the Web Insights Logs page.
See image.
To learn more, see Web Insights Logs: Columns and Web Insights Logs: Filters.

The Top AI/ML Detection Source by Security Incidents widget and the AI/ML Detection Source field are added to the Threat Incidents table and Details tab.
See image.
To learn more, see About Cybersecurity Insights.

You can use the filter AI/ML Detection Source when configuring an NSS or Cloud NSS feed for web logs.

Additionally, you can add the field %s{ai_ml_detection_src} to the Feed Output Format.
To learn more, see:
- Adding NSS Feeds for Web Logs
- Adding Cloud NSS Feeds for Web Logs
- NSS Feed Output Format: Web Logs

entries.title: Support for Display of Site Type for SharePoint Tenants
body: When creating a site on SharePoint, you can define the site type as Public, Private, or Communication. These site types are displayed for the sites associated with a group on the Manage SaaS Application Tenants > Components page.
See image.
To learn more, see Manage SaaS Application Components.

entries.title: Support for DLP Scan Timeout Identifiers in Web Insights Logs
body: You can filter and view logs for specific DLP identifiers of transactions that were exempted from policy enforcement due to a scan timeout.

entries.title: Support for Restoring Quarantined Files in Salesforce

entries.title: Additional Support for Predefined DLP Dictionaries in Endpoint DLP

entries.title: Enhancement to Cloud Application Instances

entries.status: Feature Available: Endpoint DLP 26.02.1.18 for Windows
entries.title: Endpoint DLP 26.02.1.18 Windows Enhancements and Fixes
body: - Support for Japanese predefined DLP dictionaries (i.e., Addresses (Japan), First Names (Japan), Full Names (Japan), Last Names (Japan)). To learn more, see Understanding Predefined DLP Dictionaries.

- Fixes an issue where Zscaler Incident Receiver evidence files larger than the 25 MB size limit were not uploaded. Now, Endpoint DLP generates a placeholder file for evidence files that exceed the limit.
- Fixes an issue where Application File Access rules were not being correctly enforced for the WhatsApp desktop application.

- Fixes an issue where background clipboard actions (such as hovering over elements in Slack) caused excessive notification messages. Alerts are now limited to one per process for the same clipboard content.

entries.title: Expanded SSPM Controls for Bitbucket
body: Advanced SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) expands its coverage for Bitbucket with 9 new SSPM controls, providing deeper visibility and stronger security posture assessment.

entries.title: Expanded SSPM Controls for Confluence
body: Advanced SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) expands its coverage for Confluence with 5 new SSPM controls, providing deeper visibility and stronger security posture assessment.

entries.title: Expanded SSPM Controls for Jira
body: Advanced SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) expands its coverage for Jira with 5 new SSPM controls, providing deeper visibility and stronger security posture assessment.

entries.title: Support for New Workday Filters and Prompts
body: You can use a new filter Last Functionally Updated to easily identify recently modified records when creating custom reports in Workday. Additionally, the prompts Starting Prompt and Ending Prompt fields provide greater control and precision when defining report parameters.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding SaaS Application Tenants.

entries.title: Increased Virtual Service Edge Instance Memory for Internet & SaaS on Amazon Web Services
body: Configuring Virtual Service Edge for Internet & SaaS (ZIA) on Amazon Web Services (AWS) requires 64 GB of instance memory.
Zscaler recommends the r7i.2xlarge instance size.
To learn more, see Configuring Virtual Service Edge for Internet & SaaS: Amazon Web Services and Configuring Virtual Service Edge for Internet & SaaS: Amazon Web Services with GWLB.

entries.title: Expanded SSPM Controls for Google Workspace
body: Advanced SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) expands its coverage for Google Workspace with 24 new SSPM controls, providing deeper visibility and stronger security posture assessment. The Cloud Identity license must be assigned to the Google Workspace Admin onboarding the account. This is critical to ensure appropriate license and compliance with Google Cloud Identity and Workspace policies. Additional API scopes are required for existing tenants to view the new Cloud Identity policies.
To learn more, see Adding SaaS Application Tenants.

entries.title: Gen AI Prompt Configuration for QuillBot and Google AI
body: Zscaler's Gen AI prompt configuration is extended to the QuillBot and Google AI generative AI applications. You can enable prompts for these generative AI applications to categorize and store the prompts for the respective applications.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Advanced Policy Settings.
# Added QuillBot and Google AI Capabilities to URL & Cloud App Control Policy Settings Endpoint

Two new Boolean fields, enableQuillbotAIPrompt and enableGoogleAIPrompt, are available for the AdvancedUrlFilteringCloudAppOptions model in the /advancedUrlFilterAndCloudAppSettings APIs. These fields allow users to use generative AI prompts with QuillBot and Google AI.
To learn more, see URL & Cloud App Control Policy Settings.

entries.title: Policy Level Gen AI Prompt Configuration
body: You can capture end user prompts for generative AI applications from the Cloud Application Control policy. This allows granular control of Gen AI prompt configuration. As part of this update, the Capture Prompts option is added to the Add/Edit AI & ML Rule window (Policies > Access Control > Internet & SaaS > Policies > Cloud App Control Policy > Add > AI & ML Applications).
This is applicable for Gen AI applications that are supported in the Gen AI Prompt Configuration section of the Advanced Policy Settings page.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding an AI & ML Applications Rule for Cloud App Control.
# Update to the Cloud App Control Policy Endpoint

A new Boolean field, promptCaptureEnabled, is available for the WebApplicationRule model in the /webApplicationRules APIs. This field enables users to allow or block the capture of end user prompts for generative AI applications.
To learn more, go to the WebApplicationRule model from Cloud App Control Policy.

entries.title: Adaptive Access Profiles Endpoints
body: You can retrieve a list of Adaptive Access profiles and information about an Adaptive Access profile using the following endpoints:
- GET /adaptiveAccessProfiles
- GET /adaptiveAccessProfiles/profiles/rules
To learn more about each endpoint, see the API Reference and API Rate Limit Summary.

entries.title: Enabling Incident Forwarding for Slack Chats
body: Zscaler is now forwarding Slack chat-based DLP policy incidents to the Zscaler Incident Response and Zscaler Workflow Automation along with already supported file-based violations. These incidents are also sent to Web Insights and Logs and to the respective DLP policy's auditor.

To learn more, see Understanding SaaS Security API Supported Capabilities, Configuring the Data at Rest Scanning DLP Policy with Content Inspection and Configuring the Data at Rest Scanning DLP Policy without Content Inspection.

entries.title: Updates to Azure Integration Endpoints
body: You can retrieve the progress summary of the VPN connection refresh process and start a new asynchronous process to refresh the VPN connection status using the following endpoints:
- GET /azure/refreshConnectionStatus
- POST azure/refreshConnectionStatus

You can retrieve the tunnel configuration status, start the tunnel configuration process, remove the tunnel configuration, and retrieve the status of the tunnel configuration removal process for a specified Azure hub using the following endpoints:
- GET /azure/tunnelConfiguration
- POST /azure/tunnelConfiguration
- DELETE /azure/unConfigureTunnel/{hubId}
- GET /azure/unConfigureTunnelStatus
You can retrieve the Azure hub sync process details and start a process to sync the hubs using the following endpoints:
- GET /azure/virtualHubs
- GET /azure/virtualHubSync
- POST azure/virtualHubSync
To learn more about each endpoint, see the API Reference and API Rate Limit Summary.

- PUT /alertRuleConfiguration/uebaRules/{id}
- DELETE /alertRuleConfiguration/uebaRules/{id}

- POST /alertRuleConfiguration/webhooks/test
To learn more about each endpoint, see the API Reference and API Rate Limit Summary.

entries.title: NSS Support for Admin Audit, Authentication Service Authentication, and Authentication Service SCIM Logs
body: The following enhancements are available for the NSS Feeds and Cloud NSS Feeds:

- New log types, Authentication Service Authentication and Authentication Service SCIM, are added to the NSS for Web type. These log types provide support for the Authentication Service Authentication and Authentication Service SCIM audit log reports.
- A new application filter, Authentication Service Admin Audit Log, is added to the Admin Audit Logs.
To enable these NSS Feeds and Cloud NSS Feeds enhancements, contact Zscaler Support.
To learn more, see:
- Adding NSS Feeds for Authentication Service Authentication Logs
- Adding Cloud NSS Feeds for Authentication Service Authentication Logs
- Adding NSS Feeds for Authentication Service SCIM Logs
- Adding Cloud NSS Feeds for Authentication Service SCIM Logs
- Adding NSS Feeds for Admin Audit Logs
- Adding Cloud NSS Feeds for Admin Audit Logs

entries.title: DLP Support for New PII Dictionaries
body: The following are new predefined DLP dictionaries:
- Argentina Uniform Bank Code: Detect Leakage of CBU
- Cambodian National ID: Detect Leakage of Khmer Identification Code (KIdC)
- Mexico Business Tax ID: Detect Leakage of BRFC
- Mexico Individual Tax ID: Detect Leakage of IRFC
- Mexico Social Security Number: Detect Leakage of NSS
To learn more, see Understanding Predefined DLP Dictionaries.

entries.title: Support for Collaboration Scope for Microsoft Teams
body: When creating a DLP rule for Microsoft Teams, you can define the collaboration scope as External, Internal, or Any to scan messages and attachments in channels containing external, internal, or any (internal or external) members.
See image.
On the SaaS Security Analytics page, files from MS Teams that violate the DLP policy now show their collaboration scope, among other details.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring the Data at Rest Scanning DLP Policy with Content Inspection and Configuring the Data at Rest Scanning DLP Policy without Content Inspection.

entries.title: Support for Smartsheet as an API-Based Platform in Advanced SSPM
body: Advanced SSPM supports Smartsheet as an API-based platform to provide visibility into posture misconfigurations. You can onboard a Smartsheet tenant from the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal.
See image.
To learn more, see Integrating with Smartsheet and Connecting Your Platforms to Advanced SSPM.

entries.title: Enhancement to Atlassian Integration in 3rd-Party App Governance
body: The Add Integration window for Atlassian in 3rd-Party App Governance is enhanced to allow you to enter the Atlassian subdomain and API token while adding the integration. This reduces the number of steps and simplifies the integration process to improve the user experience.
See image.
To learn more, see Integrating with Atlassian.

entries.title: Add or Remove NTP Servers Using CLI
body: You can add or remove custom NTP servers from the configuration files using CLI commands. This prevents syntax errors and duplicate entries in the configuration files.
To learn more, see Configuring Virtual Service Edge for Internet & SaaS and NTP Server Synchronization.

entries.title: Default Rules for Advanced Sandbox
body: If your organization is subscribed to the Advanced Sandbox package, the following default rules are available:
- Sandbox_Docs_Trusted
- Rule Order: 1
- Admin Rank: 7
- Rule Name: Sandbox_Docs_Trusted
- Rule Status: Disabled
- File Types: Microsoft Office (group) & PDF
- Sandbox Categories: All
- Protocols: FTP over HTTP, HTTP, HTTPS, Native FTP
- First-Time Action: Allow & Scan
- AI Instant Verdict: Enabled
- Action for Subsequent Downloads: Block

- Description: Advanced Sandbox Documents rule created during company creation. This policy rule is intended to be used with a custom user-defined URL Category Trusted Sites (or other applicable name), which after creation needs to be added to the policy via the URL Category control. This policy rule intentionally does not subject documents coming from Trusted Sites to the same level of inspection as untrusted sites.
- Sandbox_Docs_Archives
- Rule Order: 2
- Admin Rank: 7
- Rule Name: Sandbox_Docs_Archives
- Rule Status: Disabled
- File Types: Microsoft Office (group), PDF, and Archives (group)
- Sandbox Categories: All
- Protocols: FTP over HTTP, HTTP, HTTPS, Native FTP
- First-Time Action: Quarantine
- AI Instant Verdict: Enabled
- Action for Subsequent Downloads: Block
- Description: Advanced Sandbox Documents and Archives rule created during company creation. This rule must apply to all URL categories other than the custom user-defined URL Category Trusted Sites.
- Sandbox_Exes_Web
- Rule Order: 3
- Admin Rank: 7
- Rule Name: Sandbox_Exes_Web
- Rule Status: Disabled
- File Types: Executable (group), Web Content (group)
- Sandbox Categories: All
- Protocols: FTP over HTTP, HTTP, HTTPS, Native FTP
- First-Time Action: Quarantine
- AI Instant Verdict: Enabled
- Action for Subsequent Downloads: Block
- Description: Advanced Sandbox Executables and Web Content rule created during company creation.
These rules are disabled by default and can be enabled and updated to suit your organization's needs.
To learn more, see About Sandbox.

entries.title: DLP Rule Name Support for Web DLP Reports and Insights
body: Users can schedule Web DLP incident reports by DLP Rule Name to improve visibility and monitor incident counts in the Zscaler Admin Console:
Data Type DLP Rule Name is introduced in the Interactive Reports widgets and Web Insights.
See image.
To learn more, see Web Data Types and Filters.

entries.title: Document Classification and Logging for Email DLP Insights
body: AI or machine language classification is extended to support around 200 new document types across 10 common document categories.

As part of this extended support, Email DLP Insights Logs and the Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) are enhanced to provide enriched auto-classification of documents that are uploaded or downloaded during transactions.
The following enhancements are available in the Zscaler Admin Console:
# Updates to Email DLP Insights Logs

A new filter and column, Subdocument Type, is added to the Email DLP Insights Logs to capture, categorize, and log document subtypes related to administrative documents, invoices, expense reports, and more.
See image.
To learn more, see Email DLP Insights Logs: Columns and Email DLP Insights Logs: Filters.
# Updates to NSS Feeds
The field %s{ac_doc_subtypes} can be added to the Feed Output Format when configuring an NSS or Cloud NSS feed for Email DLP logs.
To learn more, see NSS Feed Output Format: Email DLP Logs.

entries.title: Enhancements to Predefined O365 One Click rule in SSL/TLS Inspection Policy
body: You can choose Evaluate Other Policies or Bypass Other Policies under the Do Not Inspect action in the O365 One Click predefined rule in the SSL/TLS Inspection Policy. This allows you to configure the predefined O365 One Click rule to either evaluate other policies (i.e., URL Filtering and Cloud App Control) or bypass them.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring SSL/TLS Inspection Policy.

entries.title: Exclude Selected URL Classes & Categories from NSS Feeds
body: Filters to include or exclude selected URL classes, URL categories, and URL super categories have been added to NSS and Cloud NSS feeds for web logs. When configuring a feed, you can select the respective URL classes and categories and include them in the logs by default or choose to exclude them from the logs.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding NSS Feeds for Web Logs and Adding Cloud NSS Feeds for Web Logs.
# Enhancement to the Cloud Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) API
New fields urlCategoriesExclude, urlClassesExclude, and urlSuperCategoriesExclude are available for the ZmanageNssFeed model in the /nssFeeds APIs.
To learn more, go to the ZmanageNssFeed model from Cloud Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS).

entries.title: New Network Applications in Firewall Control
body: The Zscaler service extends support to identify two new network applications, namely Kafka (Application Service category) and Zalo (Instant Messaging category). You can view these apps on the Network Applications page and configure them in Firewall Filtering rules to identify and manage associated traffic.
See image.
To learn more, see About Network Applications.

entries.title: Support for Cloud NSS Feeds for Alerts
body: You can configure a separate Cloud NSS feed for alerts, enabling you to monitor your Cloud NSS feeds for data lag, data loss, and the connection to your cloud-based security information and event management (SIEM) system.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding Cloud NSS Feeds for Alerts.

entries.title: API Session Timeout
body: When configuring advanced settings (Policies > Common Configuration > Advanced > Advanced Settings), you can specify how long API-initiated sessions can be inactive before they are forced to reauthenticate. The timeout duration can range from 5 to 20 minutes.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Advanced Settings.
# Enhancement to the Advanced Settings API
A new field, apiSessionTimeout, is available for the AdvancedSettings model in the /advancedSettings APIs.
To learn more, go to the AdvancedSettings model from Advanced Settings.

entries.title: Subdocument Type Support in Data Discovery Report
body: The Data Discovery Report is enhanced to include subdocument type support, providing enhanced visibility via an interactive bubble chart for ML categories. This chart utilizes nested bubbles to represent granular subdocument types, such as tax forms and legal contracts. By drilling down, users can access an expanded 4-column view where a new Subcategory column displays these specific subdocument classifications.
See image.
To learn more see, About the Data Discovery Report and Viewing Data Discovery Details.

entries.title: Update to Workload Groups Endpoints
body: You can delete a list of workload groups for an organization using the DELETE /workloadGroups endpoint. To learn more, go to DELETE /workloadGroups from Workload Groups.
To learn more about each endpoint, see the API Reference and API Rate Limit Summary.

entries.title: Browser Extension for Zero Trust Browser
body: Browser Extension for Zero Trust Browser is a lightweight solution providing seamless and secure enterprise access from any browser. The extension enhances existing browsers with browser detection and response (BDR) and browser-native data loss prevention (DLP) capabilities as well as posture-based application access.
To learn more, see Understanding Browser Extension.

entries.title: Enhancement to Advanced Threat Protection Policy
body: Advanced Threat Protection now enables users to allow the Web Proxy Auto-Discovery (WPAD) protocol from external sources to automatically discover proxy settings by locating PAC files via DHCP or DNS queries. To learn more, see Configuring the Advanced Threat Protection Policy.

entries.title: Memory Requirement for Standalone Deployment of Virtual Service Edge for Internet & SaaS
body: A stand-alone deployment of Virtual Service Edges for Internet & SaaS (ZIA) on all platforms (i.e., VMware ESXi, Microsoft Azure, AWS EC2, Microsoft Hyper-V, and GCP) requires a minimum of 48 GB of memory.
To learn more, see About Virtual Service Edges for Internet & SaaS.

body: You can update and retrieve information about the DLP Advanced Settings using the following endpoints:
- GET /webDlpGlobalOptions
- PUT /webDlpGlobalOptions
To learn more about each endpoint, see the API Reference and API Rate Limit Summary.

To learn more about each endpoint, see the API Reference and API Rate Limit Summary.

entries.title: Updates to Root Certificates and Intermediate CA Certificates Endpoints
