entries.title: Outbound Email DLP Quarantine with Release or Delete Emails in Workflow Automation
body: Zscaler now supports the Quarantine action when configuring Outbound Email DLP policies for Microsoft Exchange. When Quarantine is selected, emails that match policy criteria are quarantined directly in Microsoft Exchange. To use the Quarantine feature, go to Policy > Email DLP and then select Quarantine under Action in the applicable policy rule.
See image.

Email Data Loss Prevention (DLP) incidents that Microsoft has quarantined are displayed in Workflow Automation. In Workflow Automation, you can release or delete the email to one or more of its recipients using one of the following methods:
- On the Incident Details page, an admin can select the Release Email Quarantine action from the Actions drop-down menu and select the recipients to release the email to or delete the email.
- See image.

- When an end user responds to a user notification or escalation notification that is associated with a quarantined email incident, the notifications are enhanced to include a new Release Email to Recipients section that includes release quarantine options.
To enable this feature for Workflow Automation, contact Zscaler Support.
To learn more, see:
- About Outbound Email Policy
- Configuring Outbound Email Policy Rules
- Step-by-Step Configuration Guide for Zscaler Outbound Email DLP
- Configuring Microsoft Exchange for Zscaler Outbound Email DLP
- Adding Email Tenants
- Managing Incidents
- Viewing & Managing Incident Details

entries.title: Advanced SSPM Support for Lucidchart
body: Advanced SSPM supports a new platform, Lucidchart. You can onboard a Lucidchart tenant from the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal.
See image.
To learn more, see Connecting Your Platforms to Advanced SSPM.

entries.title: Support for Zendesk as an API-Based Platform in Advanced SSPM
body: Advanced SSPM supports Zendesk as an API-based platform. You can onboard a Zendesk tenant from the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal.
See image.
To learn more, see Connecting Your Platforms to Advanced SSPM.

entries.title: Document Classification and Logging for SaaS Security API, Email, and Endpoint DLP
body: AI or machine language classification is extended to support around 200 new document types across 10 common document categories.

As part of this extended support, Insights Logs and the Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) are enhanced to provide enriched auto-classification of documents that are uploaded or downloaded during transactions.
The following enhancements are available in the ZIA Admin Portal:
# Updates to Insights Logs

A new filter and column, Subdocument Type, is added to the Endpoint DLP Insights Logs and SaaS Security Insights Logs pages for email applications (e.g., Gmail) to capture, categorize, and log document subtypes related to administrative documents, invoices, expense reports, and more.
See image.
To learn more, see Endpoint DLP Insights Logs: Filters, Endpoint DLP Insights Logs: Columns, and About SaaS Security Insights Logs.

The field %s{doc_subtype} can be added to the Feed Output Format when configuring an NSS or Cloud NSS feed for Endpoint DLP logs. Additionally, the field %s{upload_doc_subtype} is available for SaaS Security feeds configured for email applications (e.g., Gmail). Both fields log the subtype (e.g., Financial Statements: Income Statements (Profit and Loss Statements)) of uploaded or downloaded documents.
To learn more, see NSS Feed Output Format: Endpoint DLP Logs ​​​​​​and NSS Feed Output Format: SaaS Security Logs.

body: The generative AI prompt configuration is extended to the Grammarly application, and it supports WebSocket decompression. As part of this change, the Grammarly option is added to the Policy > URL & Cloud App Control > Advanced Policy Settings page.

To learn more, see Configuring Advanced Policy Settings.

A new Boolean field, enableGrammarlyPrompt, is available for the AdvancedUrlFilteringCloudAppOptions model in the /advancedUrlFilterAndCloudAppSettings APIs. This field allows users to use generative AI prompts with Grammarly.

entries.title: Enhancements to Workload Groups
body: Workload groups allow users to search for and select tag keys discovered by the Workload Discovery Service. You must configure filters such as Source (cloud service provider), Account, Subscription, etc., to retrieve the tag keys associated with the filters. You can also manually enter custom tag keys and values for the workload groups.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Workload Groups.

entries.title: Expanded SSPM Controls for Microsoft Copilot
body: Advanced SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) expands its coverage for Microsoft Copilot with 15 new SSPM controls, providing deeper visibility and stronger security posture assessment.

entries.title: HTTP Feed Support for NSS
body: The Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) supports streaming encrypted and load-balanced NSS feeds over an HTTP connection between the NSS and your SIEM. The HTTP NSS feed uses the HTTP API to stream logs from the Zscaler nanolog cluster to your SIEM. You can configure up to 8 HTTP NSS feeds for each log type in the Zscaler Admin Console.
Also, a new action to copy your NSS feeds is added.
See image.
To learn more, see Understanding Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS), About NSS Feeds, and Adding HTTP NSS Feeds.

entries.title: Support for Microsoft Copilot Readiness Assessment
body: Organizations face a significant security risk when users inadvertently overshare or mishandle sensitive internal files. The integration of AI tools, such as Microsoft Copilot, intensifies this risk, as these tools can access information within the improperly shared files, leading to the potential exposure of sensitive data to unauthorized parties. Therefore, implementing proactive monitoring and control measures is crucial to safeguard organizational security and prevent accidental data leaks.
As part of this feature, the following enhancements are available in the Zscaler Admin Console:
# SaaS Workflows: Microsoft Copilot Readiness Assessment

SaaS Workflows is introduced to streamline data protection and compliance, which is designed to automate processes and enable bulk remediation actions. A significant current capability within these workflows is the new Microsoft Copilot Readiness Assessment page. This is crucial in helping organizations mitigate risks and guarantee a secure and prepared onboarding experience for Microsoft applications.
You can access the dashboard from Analytics > Internet & SaaS > Analytics > SaaS Workflows > Microsoft Copilot Readiness Assessment.
See image.
To learn more, see About SaaS Workflows, About Microsoft Copilot Readiness Assessment, and Viewing Drill Down of All Assets.
# SaaS Security Insights Logs and SaaS Security Assets Logs

Filters and columns, Accessibility Flags and Label, are added to the SaaS Security Insights Logs page and SaaS Security Assets with Incidents page (Analytics > Internet & SaaS > Analytics > SaaS Security > Assets) for collaboration applications, email applications, and file sharing applications.
See image.
To learn more, see About SaaS Security Insights Logs and Understanding the Assets Report: Assets with Incidents.
# NSS Feeds

You can add the following fields for the Microsoft Copilot Readiness Assessment when configuring SaaS Security NSS or Cloud NSS Feed Output Format. These fields apply to collaboration, email, and file applications:
- %s{labelname}
- %s{accessibility_flags}
- %s{copilot_accessible}
To learn more, see NSS Feed Output Format: SaaS Security Logs.

entries.title: Support for Workday Tenant RaaS-based API Access
body: Workday tenants now support RaaS-based API access which enables secure, programmatic retrieval of data and management through web services. Existing Workday tenants need to be reauthenticated by editing the tenant and revalidating.
To learn more, see Adding SaaS Application Tenants and About SaaS Application Tenants.

entries.title: Support in SaaS Security Data at Rest DLP Policy for Quarantine of Sensitive Content in Microsoft Teams
body: The SaaS Security Data at Rest Scanning policy supports a new option to quarantine sensitive content in Microsoft Teams. You can specify a tombstone message that end users see when messages or files in Microsoft Teams are quarantined.
See image.
After a message or file has been quarantined in Microsoft Teams, admins can use the SaaS Assets Report to review and remove the quarantined content.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring the SaaS Security API DLP Policy, About Quarantine Tombstone File Templates, and SaaS Assets Report: Assets with Incidents.

entries.title: Cloud Custom IPS Enhancements
body: Custom IPS is supported on Zscaler's public cloud, allowing you to create and deploy custom IPS signature rules without requiring any additional infrastructure (previously required a Private Service Edge deployment). You can inspect traffic transiting the Zscaler cloud against your custom signatures, irrespective of whether it is forwarded to a Public, Private, or Virtual Service Edge.
To enable Custom IPS with your Advanced Firewall subscription, contact your Zscaler Account team.
With this upgrade, the following enhancements are also made to Custom IPS:
- Applicable to decrypted web traffic (decrypted via SSL Inspection) in addition to non-web traffic.
- Extended support for HTTP protocol-aware signatures, so signature rules can include HTTP-specific options.

- Signature rule validation occurs in two stages before deployment: static validation (currently supported) that checks rules for syntax errors, duplication, and based on other predefined conditions; dynamic validation (newly added) that runs signatures against designated packet captures to ensure efficient resource usage and optimal performance. The signature is enabled after both validations are completed. These transitions are indicated by new statuses.
- View the newly added actions to initiate dynamic validation of signature rules.
- In the Add Signature Rule (and Edit Signature Rule) window, a Save & Promote button is added to trigger dynamic validation of the rule.
- Save image.

- The Enable Signature Rule toggle button is not accessible until the rule moves to the Enable Ready state with the successful completion of dynamic validation. There is no change to the existing Save option, which continues to save the rule after successful static validation.
- On the Custom Signature Rules page, a Promote All button is added to initiate dynamic validation of all rules at once.
- See image.
- Logs showing custom signature matches for better visibility and easier troubleshooting.
- Increased the custom signature rule limit to 1,000 (previously 500).
To learn more, see About Custom IPS Signature Rules, Configuring Custom IPS Signature Rules, and Specifications & Limitations for Custom IPS Signature Rules.

entries.title: DLP and File Type Support for RPM Files
body: The File Type Control and Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies now support RPM files in the Archive category.
- File Type Control
- DLP - Rule without Content Matching
To learn more, see About File Type Control and About Data Loss Prevention.

entries.title: Advanced SaaS Security Posture Management Support for Oracle Financials Cloud
body: You can configure Advanced SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) for Oracle Financials Cloud tenants. Select the SSPM Scan checkbox when onboarding a tenant to enable the Advanced SSPM scan capability for the specific tenant.
See image.
The SSPM Scan checkbox is enabled only when you have Advanced SSPM enabled for your tenant.
To learn more, see What Is Advanced Posture Management? and Adding SaaS Application Tenants.

entries.title: Application Investigation in Endpoint Data Scan
body: Zscaler's Application Investigation is a solution that provides comprehensive visibility and automated risk management for an organization's application ecosystem by delivering a clear view of all software in use, including unauthorized AI tools and unapproved browsers. By automatically identifying vulnerable or suspicious applications, Application Investigation enables administrators to prioritize security efforts and focus on the highest-threat categories and vulnerabilities across the organization.

The Application Investigation page (Analytics > Endpoint Data Scan > Application Investigation) provides insights into executable files and applications stored on endpoints, gathering data on installed software, running processes, and libraries. This is crucial not only for compliance, but also for monitoring, auditing, and identifying vulnerabilities or unauthorized software.
As part of this change, the Inventory > Applications tab is now moved to Application Investigation > Inventory tab.
See image.

To learn more, see About the Application Investigation Overview, About the Application Investigation Inventory, Analyzing Applications Details, and Accessing and Navigating the Endpoint Data Scan Report.

entries.title: DLP Operational in Endpoint Data Scan
body: The Zscaler DLP Operational page (Analytics > Endpoint Data Scan > DLP Operational) provides insights into the endpoint's status, thereby ensuring that the system functions properly and as designed to avoid sensitive data leakage.
See image.
To learn more, see About DLP Operational Dashboard.

entries.title: Filtering by User Group in Endpoint Data Scan
body: Administrators can filter data on the Endpoint Data Scan page (Analytics > Endpoint Data Scan > Endpoint Data Scan) by a specific user group.
See image.
To learn more, see About Endpoint Data Scan.

entries.title: New Bandwidth Control Fields for Transactions
body: Web Insights are enhanced to allow users to view the latency caused by bandwidth control on transactions in the ZIA Admin Portal.
# Web Insights Logs
The following new columns and filters are available in the Web Insights Logs:
- Request Latency Due to Bandwidth Control (ms)
- Response Latency Due to Bandwidth Control (ms)
- Total Latency Due to Bandwidth Control (ms)
See image.
To learn more, see Web Insights Logs: Columns and Web Insights Logs: Filters.
# NSS Feeds

The fields %d{txn_delay_req} and %d{txn_delay_resp} can be added to the Feed Output Format when configuring an NSS or Cloud NSS feed for web logs. These fields display the bandwidth transaction request delay and the bandwidth transaction response delay in milliseconds, respectively.
To learn more, see NSS Feed Output Format: Web Logs.

entries.title: Share Files Externally in Endpoint Data Scan
body: Share Files Externally provides a capability for Endpoint DLP that allows authorized users to securely share sensitive files with external partners by encrypting the data into a secure HTML format, ensuring that only verified recipients can access the content.
You can access the Share Files Externally page from Analytics > Endpoint Data Scan > Sensitive Information.
See image.
To learn more, see About Endpoint Data Scan Sensitive Information: Share Files Externally, Configuring Share File Externally Settings, and Understanding Share Files Externally.

entries.title: Support for CIDR and Regex on Network Share DLP Resources
body: The Zscaler service supports using Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) ranges and regular expressions for advanced matching when creating or editing network shares for Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) resources. The following image shows a regular expression that matches all network servers that start with "srv" and the match is case insensitive:
See Image.
To learn more, see Adding DLP Resources and Editing DLP Resources.

entries.title: Support for Network Type on Endpoint DLP Policy Rules
body: The Zscaler service supports specifying a network type (e.g., Trusted, Off-Trusted, VPN) for the Network Share, Printing, and Device Control channels when creating policy rules for Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP).
- Endpoints must be running Zscaler Client Connector version 4.8.600 or later (Windows) or version 4.7.1 or later (macOS) for policy rules to enforce the network type.
- To enable this feature, contact your Zscaler Account team.
See Image.
To learn more, see Configuring Endpoint DLP Policy Rules and About Trusted Networks.

entries.title: Exact Data Matching in Endpoint Data Scan
body: Zscaler has introduced Exact Data Matching (EDM) for Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) which provides protection for structured sensitive data. This feature utilizes a unique hybrid architecture where the endpoint performs local prefiltering to identify candidate files for cloud inspection, ensuring maximum accuracy without compromising device performance or bandwidth.
You can access Exact Data Matching (EDM) page from Analytics > Endpoint Data Scan > Sensitive Information.
To enable this feature, contact your Zscaler Account team.
See image.
To learn more, see Understanding Exact Data Matching (EDM) and About Endpoint Data Scan Sensitive Information: Exact Data Matching.

entries.title: Enhancement to Firewall Policies Endpoints

The ruleLabelId query parameter allows you to filter Firewall Filtering rules based on the rule label ID. To learn more, go to GET /firewallFilteringRules and GET /firewallFilteringRules/count from Firewall Policies.

entries.title: Support for Certificate-based Authentication with Microsoft Applications for a Custom Zscaler Connector
body: When you create a custom Zscaler connector for a Microsoft application, you have the option to choose whether you want to provide a client secret or a private key in the Zscaler Admin Console so that the Zscaler service can access the application. SharePoint, Copilot, and Microsoft 365 require a private key for onboarding, but all other supported Microsoft applications support both options.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding SaaS Application Tenants and Authorizing a Custom Zscaler Connector for Microsoft Applications.

To learn more about each endpoint, see the API Reference and API Rate Limit Summary.

entries.title: Introducing Flexible Permission Selection for SSPM Connectors
body: The SaaS application tenants GitHub, Jira, Okta, Confluence, Trello, Webex Teams, and Google Workspace now have the option to onboard for SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) scan by choosing Read-only or Read/Write (full access) for the connector role. The Read/Write connector role is the default option.

This enhancement removes the friction caused by shared DLP and SSPM connectors that previously required elevated permissions for posture-only use cases. Administrators can onboard applications with minimal, least-privilege access for SSPM posture assessments and later upgrade to full permissions only if they choose to enable DLP content scanning or posture remediation. This provides a more secure, flexible, and customer-friendly onboarding experience.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding SaaS Application Tenants and Permissions for Onboarding SaaS Apps for SSPM.

entries.title: Enhancements to Endpoint DLP for macOS
body: The following enhancements are available in Zscaler Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) for macOS:
# Support for Endpoint DLP Block Action for Printing on macOS
The Zscaler service supports the Block action for printing from macOS devices in Endpoint DLP rules with content inspection.
See Image.
To learn more, see Configuring Endpoint DLP Policy Rules.
# Endpoint DLP Support for Clipboard and Application File Access
To access this feature, contact your Zscaler Account team.
Endpoint DLP supports monitoring and blocking sensitive information when specific applications access files, as well as when content is pasted into those applications.
To get started, configure the relevant applications to prevent sensitive data loss on the DLP Resources page (Policies > Data Protection > Policy > Endpoint Controls > Endpoint DLP Resources):
See Image.
After applications are defined, you can create Endpoint DLP policy rules that:
- Protect file access: Use Application File Access as the channel to detect and block sensitive data exposed when applications read files.
- Protect clipboard activity: Use Clipboard as the channel to detect and block sensitive data pasted into applications.
See Image.
To learn more, see About DLP Resources, Adding DLP Resources and Configuring Endpoint DLP Policy Rules.
# Removable Storage Rule: Device Per User Pair

Streamline management of the Device Control Removable Storage rules by defining multiple removable storage devices and mapping them to specific users or endpoints within a single rule. This rule also supports CSV file import for bulk operations.
See Image.
To learn more, see Managing a Removable Storage Rule.
# Endpoint Data Scan: End User Report

This feature introduces configurable reports to increase transparency for end users. These reports aim at providing users with best practices and show them where sensitive data is stored locally on their endpoints. This feature aims at making endpoint data scanning more efficient, transparent, and collaborative, improving how administrators and end users work together to manage sensitive data.
To learn more, see Understanding End User Reports, About Endpoint Data Scan, and Analyzing Endpoint DLP Scan for a User.
# Endpoint DLP Configurations
This feature introduces the following expanded configuration options across Endpoint Data Scan, Classification, and DLP inspection to improve performance, control, and flexibility:
- Endpoint Data Scan
- Granular controls for End User report visibility, scheduling, sensitive data exposure, and custom messages.
- Ability to exclude specific file systems, folders, and entities.
- Classification Settings
- Configurable maximum file size and timeout strategies with Allow or Block fallback actions.
- Other Enhancements
- Option to hide the Protect action for end users.
- Controls for Application Inventory Scan.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Endpoint Data Scan and Endpoint Settings and Activating Device Control Policy Rules and Configuration Changes.
# Sensitive Information Index Document Match
To access this feature, contact your Zscaler Account team.

This new capability allows for the detection of data exfiltration on Endpoint DLP channels by matching full or partial content against indexed documents. A secure, endpoint-based workflow has been introduced in this release, enabling authorized users to index sensitive documents directly from their endpoints using the Endpoint DLP context menu. The Endpoint Index Document Match (IDM) operates in parallel to the Inline DLP IDM. Enforcement and detection are independent and require reindexing of IDM files using the Endpoint DLP. This feature is currently in limited availability. You can access the Sensitive Information page from Analytics > Data Security > Endpoint.
See image.
To learn more, see About Sensitive Information and Configuring Sensitive Information Settings.
# Additional Support for Predefined DLP Dictionaries in Endpoint DLP
The following predefined DLP dictionaries are supported for use in Endpoint DLP policy rules:
- CNPJ Number (Brazil)
- International Bank Account Number (IBAN)
- National Economic Registry Number (Poland)
- Passport Number (Asia)
To learn more, see Understanding Predefined DLP Dictionaries.
# Added Context for Endpoint DLP Triggers

You can see an additional 15-byte prefix and suffix to the left and right of the Endpoint DLP trigger that provides more information about the Endpoint DLP incident. The additional context can be seen in the Incident Receiver, Zscaler Workflow Automation, and Email Notifications.
The following image shows an example of trigger context in Zscaler Workflow Automation:
See image.

To learn more, see Configuring DLP Notification Templates, Configuring the Zscaler Incident Receiver for On-Premises VMs, Configuring the Zscaler Incident Receiver for Amazon Web Services EC2 VMs, and Configuring the Zscaler Incident Receiver for Azure VMs.
# Endpoint DLP Support for Proximity Length in Predefined Dictionaries

The Zscaler service supports the Proximity Length field on applicable predefined DLP dictionaries when used in engines associated with Endpoint DLP rules. The proximity length defines how close a high confidence phrase must be to an instance of the pattern (that the dictionary detects) to count as a match. For certain predefined DLP dictionaries, the Proximity Length field appears when the dictionary’s Confidence Score Threshold is High.
See Image.
To learn more, see Understanding Predefined DLP Dictionaries.

entries.title: Security Fixes
body: Proper neutralization of user input in specific input fields in the ZIA Admin Portal no longer allows an authenticated administrator to access unauthorized internal information in rare conditions (CVE-2026-22568).

entries.title: Advanced SaaS Security Posture Management Support for JumpCloud
body: You can configure Advanced SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) for JumpCloud tenants. Select the SSPM Scan checkbox when onboarding a JumpCloud tenant to enable the Advanced SSPM scan capability for the specific tenant.
See image.
The SSPM Scan checkbox is enabled only when you have Advanced SSPM enabled for your tenant.
To learn more, see What Is Advanced Posture Management? and Adding SaaS Application Tenants.

entries.title: Insights Logs Improvements & Enhancements
body: The Insights Logs pages now feature asynchronous log retrieval. This enhancement allows users to continue working without interruption while queries are executed in the background, significantly improving their user experience.
The following enhancements are available for Insights Logs in the ZIA Admin Portal:

- You can initiate log queries or move active searches to the background with Export in Background option, so you can continue other administrative tasks without interruption. The query is not terminated while running in the background, and a progress bar is displayed. During this process, you can choose to keep the query active, move it to the background, or stop the execution entirely.
- The Apply Filters button is renamed to Run Query to better reflect the action.
- You can export up to 1 million records to a CSV file and view up to 25,000 records directly in the portal.
- You can specify a custom name for the downloaded CSV file for better organization.
- Each admin can only run one asynchronous query at a time.
- Only the user who initiated the query can view the results on-screen or access the downloaded file.
See image.
To learn more, see About Insights Logs.

See image.

entries.title: Advanced SSPM Support for Bitwarden

entries.title: Sandbox Verdict Logging
body: Zscaler supports comprehensive logging of Sandbox analysis activities through Insights Logs and the Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS). You can log and view details of all files that went through behavioral analysis regardless of the verdict (e.g., Suspicious Content, Benign). With the following enhancements in the ZIA Admin Portal, you can find the relevant details quickly in order to triage and address the event appropriately:
# Sandbox Verdict Insights Logs
With the new Sandbox Verdict Insights page (Analytics > Sandbox Verdict Insights), you can view recent sandbox analysis activity logs.
See image.
To learn more, see About Insights, About Insights Logs, Sandbox Verdict Insights Logs: Filters, and Sandbox Verdict Insights Logs: Columns.
# NSS Feeds

A new log type, Sandbox Verdict, is available for NSS. You can configure an NSS feed or Cloud NSS feed to stream Sandbox analysis data from Zscaler to your security information and event management (SIEM) system.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding NSS Feeds for Sandbox Verdict Logs, Adding Cloud NSS Feeds for Sandbox Verdict Logs, and NSS Feed Output Format: Sandbox Verdict Logs.

entries.title: Enhancement to Extranet Application Support
body: Extranet Application Support can be configured bidirectionally, allowing partners to access your organization's resources securely.
Extranet Application Support is a feature in limited availability. To access Extranet Application Support, contact your Zscaler Account team.
As part of this enhancement:
- Custom IP pools can be configured for Extranet Application Support.
- See image.
- Static IP addresses, GRE tunnels, and sublocations are configurable for extranet locations.
- Firewall Control is automatically enabled for extranet locations.
- IPS Control is available for extranet locations.
- Three default policy rules are added to the Forwarding Control policy when Extranet Application Support is enabled.
- See image.
- One predefined policy rule is added to the DNS Control policy when Extranet Application Support is enabled.
- See image.
To learn more, see Understanding Extranet Application Support.
# Insights Logs
A filter and column, Extranet Resource, is added to DNS Insights Logs, Firewall Insights Logs, and Web Insights Logs.
See image.

To learn more, see DNS Insights Logs: Columns, DNS Insights Logs: Filters, Firewall Insights Logs: Columns, Firewall Insights Logs: Filters, Web Insights Logs: Columns, and Web Insights Logs: Filters.
# NSS Logs
- The field %s{extranet_name} is available when adding an NSS feed or Cloud NSS feed for Web, Firewall, and DNS logs.
- To learn more, see NSS Feed Output Format: Web Logs, NSS Feed Output Format: Firewall Logs, and NSS Feed Output Format: DNS Logs.
- For NSS or Cloud NSS feed Tunnel logs, when configuring the Tunnel Type filter, you can select EAS Client Tunnel to limit the logs based on this tunnel type.
- See image.
- To learn more, see Adding NSS Feeds for Tunnel Logs and Adding Cloud NSS Feeds for Tunnel Logs.

entries.title: Authentication Service Integration for Management Portal for Partners & Other Enhancements
body: The Zscaler service supports Authentication Service Single Sign-On (SSO) for partner logins to the Zscaler Management Portal for Partners. Following the migration, all partner logins route through the Authentication Service SSO framework, offering a secure and unified authentication experience.
For partners migrated to Authentication Service, the following features move under Authentication Service:
- Role and Scope Assignments: To assign a role or scope to admins, go to Authentication Service Admin Portal > Administration > Entitlements.
- Password Resets: To reset a password, go to Authentication Service Admin Portal > Administration.
See image.
Further, we are also introducing a new way to manage tenants and admins: scopes. Scopes are multi-tenant, multi-cloud setups that you can assign to one or more admins, as required.
To learn more, see About Scopes, Adding a New Scope, and Assigning Entitlements to Users and User Groups.

entries.title: Enhanced Flexibility in the URL Filtering Policy Rule Creation
body: You can apply either OR or AND logical operator between the Users, Groups, and Departments criteria in the URL Filtering Policy rules. This allows you to create granular policy rules using a combination of logical operators (i.e., OR or AND) between these criteria. As part of this update, up and down arrows are added to the logical operators between these criteria in the Add/Edit URL Filtering Rule window.
To enable this feature, contact Zscaler Support.

You can also add up to three Groups fields by clicking the Add icon next to the Groups field, and they are connected with a logical AND operator. This allows you to create rules that are triggered when they match the selected groups in all the Groups fields.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring the URL Filtering Policy.
# Enhancement to URL Filtering Policy Endpoints
New fields, usersAndGroupsSet, groupsAndDepartmentsSet, groups2, and groups3 are available for the UrlFilteringRule model in the /urlFilteringRules APIs.
To learn more, go to the UrlFilteringRule model from URL Filtering Policy.

entries.title: Enhancement to Zscaler Cloud Performance Test Tool
body: The Zscaler Cloud Performance Test Tool allows you to view only the domain part of the traffic or email, and the user name is hidden. For example, johndoe@zscaler.com is visible as xxxxxxx@zscaler.com.
See image.
To learn more, see Using the Zscaler Cloud Performance Test Tool.

entries.title: Increased AWS Account IDs in Tenant Profiles
body: You can add up to 512 account IDs per tenant profile for AWS and there can be a maximum of 4,096 account IDs across all profiles.
To learn more, see Adding Tenant Profiles and Ranges & Limitations.

After deploying an NSS VM, you can stream your organization’s web or firewall logs from the Zscaler cloud to your security information and event management (SIEM) system.

entries.title: NSS Support for Nutanix
body: Zscaler’s Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) supports the configuration and deployment of an NSS virtual machine (VM) on Nutanix.
After deploying an NSS VM, you can stream your organization’s Web or Firewall logs from the Zscaler cloud to your security information and event management system.
See image.

entries.title: Update to Admin Audit Logs and Event Logs API Endpoints
body: When you request report generation using POST /auditlogEntryReport or POST /eventlogEntryReport, it returns an HTTP 200 OK status code with the statusId in the response (previously returned 204 status code). This statusId must be captured and sent as a query parameter in the following requests that are subsequently made to check the report status, download the report, or cancel the report request:
- GET /auditlogEntryReport
- GET /auditlogEntryReport/download
- DELETE /auditlogEntryReport
- GET /eventlogEntryReport
- GET /eventlogEntryReport/download
- DELETE /eventlogEntryReport

This API workflow change requires you to update your existing scripts immediately to ensure that your automated integrations for downloading audit and event logs continue to function correctly. Modify your scripts to parse the statusId from the initial report generation response and ensure that your API requests to check status, download, or cancel are updated to pass the statusId parameter.
To learn more, see the API Reference and Downloading Audit Logs and Event Logs Using API.

entries.title: Enhancements to 3rd-Party App Governance and Advanced SSPM
body: The following enhancements are available in 3rd-Party App Governance and Advanced SSPM:
## Settings
The SaaS Tenants and Notifications tabs are added to the Settings page. These tabs allow you to view and manage the onboarded SaaS tenants and also configure Slack and email notifications.
See image.
To learn more, see About Settings in 3rd-Party App Governance.
## Connect Drop-Down Menu
A drop-down menu is added under the Connect button on the App Dashboard. From this drop-down menu, you can select the platform you want to connect to 3rd-Party App Governance or Advanced SSPM.
See image.
To learn more, see Connecting Your Platforms to 3rd-Party App Governance and Connecting Your Platforms to Advanced SSPM.

entries.title: Sandboxing Password-Protected PDF Files for Isolation
body: Zscaler Isolation now supports password-protected PDF files to be sandboxed for Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA). If ZIA Sandbox determines that the file is safe, users can download the original PDF. If ZIA Sandbox determines that the file is malicious, users cannot download the original PDF to their local device, and Zscaler stores the password for the duration of the isolated session. If the PDF can be rendered within the isolated browser, users can download the sanitized version of the PDF.

After the PDF is downloaded into the Isolation container, it opens on the user's device automatically, and they are prompted for the file password. Users are allowed unlimited incorrect password attempts.
To learn more, see About Sandbox Integration with Isolation and Transferring and Viewing Files in Isolation.

entries.title: Deprecation of SSPM Policies for Microsoft 365
body: The following policies are deprecated for Microsoft 365 in both SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) Essentials and Advanced SSPM:
- Set Automated Notifications for New and Trending Cloud Applications in Our Organization
- Set Automated Notification for New OAuth Applications Connected to Your Corporate Environment
To learn more, see Viewing and Managing the Supported SSPM Policies and What Is Advanced Posture Management?

entries.title: Enhanced Logging of Collaborator Group Members
body: This enhancement allows you to view logs for individual members within a collaborator group. As part of the update, the following changes are available in the ZIA Admin Portal:
# SaaS Security Insights Logs and SaaS Security Assets with Incidents

When an individual file is shared with a group, you can view logs for individual members of a group who are either internal collaborators or external collaborators, depending upon the type of domain they belong to in the SaaS Security Insights Logs page and the Assets Report: Assets with Incidents page (Analytics > SaaS Security > Assets > click an application or tenant).
To learn more, see About SaaS Security Insights Logs and Understanding the Assets Report: Assets with Incidents.
# SaaS Security Data at Rest Scanning DLP Actions

For file sharing applications, the DLP actions Remove Internal Collaborators, Remove External Collaborators, and Remove External Collaborators and Shareable Link also remove internal and external collaborator groups along with all individual internal and external collaborators. To remove an individual collaborator from an external group, you can use the Remove External Collaborators action on the Remediation page to manually remove the collaborator.
To learn more, see Configuring the Data at Rest Scanning DLP Policy with Content Inspection and Configuring the Data at Rest Scanning DLP Policy without Content Inspection.

entries.title: Enhancement to URL Filtering Policy Page
body: On the URL Filtering Policy page (Policy > URL & Cloud App Control > URL Filtering Policy), the URL Filtering rules are paginated with up to 100 rules displayed per page.
See image.
You can filter and search for URL Filtering rules based on the following categories:
- Rule Label
- Rule Name
- Rule Order
- Description
- Action
- Location
- Location Group
- Department
- Group
- User
- Device
- Device Group
- Source IP Group
- URL Categories
- HTTP Header Profile
See image.
To learn more, see About URL Filtering.
# Updates to the Rule Labels and URL Filtering Policy endpoint categories

You can retrieve a list of rule labels based on the specified rule type using the GET /ruleLabels/ruleType/{ruleType} endpoint and retrieve the count of URL Filtering rules using the GET urlFilteringRules/count endpoint.

Two new query parameters, page and pageSize are available for the GET /urlFilteringRules endpoint. When you do not specify the page and pageSize query parameters, the default values are used. To learn more, see Fetching URL Filtering Rules Using Pagination and Search Filters.
To learn more about each endpoint, see the API Reference and API Rate Limit Summary.

entries.title: Enhancement to Virtual Service Edges
body: The following platforms support 64 GB of RAM and 3 antivirus (AV) engines per Virtual Service Edge:
- VMware ESXi
- Microsoft Azure
- Google Cloud Platform
- Microsoft Hyper-V
- Amazon Web Services
- Amazon Web Services with GWLB
This allows you to scan large files and maintain Virtual Service Edge performance. You can deploy Virtual Service Edge either in standalone or cluster mode.

entries.title: Gen AI Prompt Obfuscation
body: Generative AI (Gen AI) prompts that are displayed in the Web Insights Logs can be obfuscated when adding admin roles.
See image.
To learn more, see About the Gen AI Security Report.

entries.title: Granular Control for Atlassian AI Application
body: You can allow or block the use of embedded AI applications on Atlassian sites and enable or disable Zscaler to store the generative AI prompts entered in these embedded AI applications per cloud app control rule. As part of this feature, the following fields appear in the Add/Edit Productivity and CRM Tools Rule window only for the Atlassian application:
- Embedded AI
- Embedded AI Prompts
See image.
To learn more, see Adding a Productivity & CRM Tools Rule for Cloud App Control.
# Web Insights Logs
An Application Activity, Embedded AI, is added to the Web Insights Logs for Atlassian applications only.
See image.
To learn more, see Web Insights Logs: Filters.

entries.title: Logs for Email Received and Sent Time
body: The following enhancements are available for Insights and NSS Feeds in the ZIA Admin Portal to record the time Zscaler either received or sent an email response.
# Insights Logs

New columns Zscaler Sent Time and Zscaler Received Time are added to Email DLP Insights Logs. The Scan Time field is enhanced to reflect the duration of time (milliseconds) from when Zscaler receives an email until the Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy evaluation is complete.
See image.
To learn more, see Email DLP Insights Logs: Columns.
# NSS Feeds

The fields %s{zs_rcv_time} and %s{zs_sent_time} can be added to the Feed Output Format when configuring NSS or Cloud NSS feeds for Email DLP logs. The %llu{scan_time} field is enhanced to reflect the duration of time (milliseconds) from when Zscaler receives an email until the DLP policy evaluation is complete.
To learn more, see NSS Feed Output Format: Email DLP Logs.

entries.title: Pattern Requirements for Custom DLP Dictionaries
body: For custom Data Loss Prevention (DLP) dictionaries that use patterns with lookaround constructs (also known as zero-length assertions), the Zscaler service now enforces the following restrictions:
- You must select Match Any Patterns and Any Phrases as the Match Type.
- You must configure at least one phrase.
To learn more, see Adding Custom DLP Dictionaries.

entries.title: Support for Adjustable Polling Intervals
body: When scheduling a scan for SaaS applications tenants (Policy > SaaS Security > Scan Configuration > Add Scan Schedule), you can also configure the polling interval based on how often you want the system to scan the application.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring SaaS Security Scan Schedules.

entries.title: Support for Number of Collaborators for File Sharing Apps in DLP
body: The SaaS Security Data at Rest Scanning Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy supports the number of internal and external collaborators as scoping criteria for all file sharing applications, including Box, Dropbox, Confluence, ShareFile, and Smartsheet. Administrators can monitor file sharing among collaborators by applying the scope to a number of internal and external collaborators.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring the Data At Rest Scanning DLP Policy and About Data at Rest Scanning DLP.

entries.title: Support for Quarantine File to Desired Location for File Sharing Apps
body: The support for quarantining files in a desired location has been extended to all file sharing apps, including Box, Dropbox, Confluence, ShareFile, and Smartsheet. This feature was already available for Google Drive, OneDrive, and SharePoint apps. You can specify a quarantine location for files violating DLP policy rules at the time of onboarding the tenant.
On the Edit DLP Rule window, a new action called Admin Quarantine is available for all tenants with a defined quarantine location.
See image.

To learn more, see About Data at Rest Scanning DLP, Configuring the Data at Rest Scanning DLP Policy with Content Inspection, and Configuring the Data at Rest Scanning DLP Policy without Content Inspection.

entries.title: Automatic Local Language Translation for Isolation in ZIA
body: Automatic language translation is globally available for Isolation. The isolated session localizes the language based on the user's browser language settings, and displays that language on the rendered web page.
To learn more, see Understanding Language Translate for Isolation.

entries.title: Original URL for Isolation Profiles in ZIA
body: Original URL has replaced Local Browser Rendering in Isolation. It is now an option that admins can configure in isolation profiles. This means that the user of the isolation profile sees the native browser URL of the web page that loads when entering Isolation.
To learn more, see User Experience Modes in Isolation and Original URL for Isolation.

entries.title: Visual Indicator for Turbo Mode in Isolation for ZIA
body: If Turbo Mode is enabled on an isolation profile and the user also has hardware acceleration enabled, the appearance of the zGPU icon next to the Turbo Mode command is displayed in the Isolation Bar.
See image.
To learn more, see Understanding Turbo Mode for Isolation.

entries.title: Updates to Firewall Dashboard and Insights
body: On the Firewall Insights page (Analytics > Firewall Insights), the maximum number of rules displayed for the Rule Name data type has been increased. When using bar or table charts, you can view up to the top 4,000 rules (in increments of 500, 1,000, 2,000, and 4,000) by selecting the value from the drop-down menu.
In addition, the charts explicitly show rules that were not triggered during the selected time frame, displaying them with a zero hit count if they fall within the specified rule limit.
See image.

The Firewall Overview dashboard includes additional time filters, allowing you to view data over 48-hour, 3-day, 5-day, and 7-day intervals. Additionally, widgets using the Rule Name data type display hit counts for all rules when viewed as bar and table charts.
In addition, the charts explicitly show rules that were not triggered during the selected time frame, displaying them with a zero hit count if they fall within the specified rule limit.
See image.

These time and value filter enhancements allow you to track rule hit counts over extended time periods, helping you analyze rule utilization and optimize or refine your firewall rule configurations based on real-world traffic patterns.

entries.title: Create VM Instance using the Virtual Service Edge Amazon Web Services Terraform Modules
body: You can create a virtual machine (VM) in Amazon Web Services (AWS) using the Virtual Service Edge Terraform modules.
To learn more, see Configuring Virtual Service Edge for Amazon Web Services and Configuring Virtual Service Edge for Amazon Web Services with GWLB.

entries.title: Gen AI Prompt Configuration for Claude and Mistral
body: Zscaler's Gen AI prompt configuration is extended to the Claude and Mistral generative AI applications. You can enable prompts for these generative AI applications to categorize and store the prompts for the respective applications.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Advanced Policy Settings.
# Added Claude and Mistral Capabilities to URL & Cloud App Control Policy Settings Endpoint

Two new Boolean fields, enableClaudePrompt and enableMistralAIPrompt, are available for the AdvancedUrlFilteringCloudAppOptions model in the /advancedUrlFilterAndCloudAppSettings APIs. These fields allow users to use generative AI prompts with Claude and Mistral.
To learn more, see URL & Cloud App Control Policy Settings.

entries.title: Enhancement to Filters in 3rd-Party App Governance and Advanced SSPM
body: In the App Inventory and User Inventory, and on the Posture page, the filter options that don't currently exist in your organization display separately and do not return results. You can still select them when creating new views and policies. If a new app in your organization matches a policy, the policy is triggered and the filter options will be included in your organization.
See image.
To learn more, see App Inventory Filters, About User Inventory, and About Posture.

entries.title: Support for GitHub User Email Enrichment in 3rd-Party App Governance
body: The Users page displays multiple emails in addition to public emails for GitHub users. These emails are associated with the domain of the organization that owns the GitHub account. This enhancement improves the ability to find user and admin emails from outside the domain.
To learn more, see About User Inventory.

entries.title: Updates to 3rd-Party App Governance API
body: The 3rd-Party App Governance API adds a new endpoint, /app_views/{appViewId}/accounts, to retrieve users' email addresses associated with specific app IDs.
/app_views/{appViewId}/apps_extended provides the total number of enabled users totalenabledusers within its response.
To learn more about this endpoint, see the Understanding ZIA APIs and API Rate Limit Summary.

entries.title: Support for Google Workspace OU Segregation
body: You can segregate your Google Workspace integration by organizational units (OUs) in 3rd-Party App Governance. This segregation ensures that each OU can access only its relevant users, applications, and posture data, while maintaining consolidated tenant management for admins.
To enable this feature, contact Zscaler Support.
To learn more, see Integrating with Google Workspace.

entries.title: Enhancements to Endpoint DLP for Windows
body: The following enhancements are available in Zscaler Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) for Windows:
# Endpoint DLP Support for Clipboard and Application File Access
To access this feature, contact your Zscaler Account team.
Endpoint DLP supports monitoring and blocking sensitive information when specific applications access files, as well as when content is pasted into those applications.
To get started, configure the relevant applications to prevent sensitive data loss on the DLP Resources page (Administration > DLP Resources):
See Image.
Once applications are defined, you can create Endpoint DLP policy rules that:
- Protect file access: Use Application File Access as the channel to detect and block sensitive data exposed when applications read files.
- Protect clipboard activity: Use Clipboard as the channel to detect and block sensitive data pasted into applications.
See Image.
To learn more, see About DLP Resources, Adding DLP Resources and Configuring Endpoint DLP Policy Rules.
# Removable Storage Rule: Device Per User Pair

Streamline management of the Device Control Removable Storage rules by defining multiple removable storage devices and mapping them to specific users or endpoints within a single rule. This rule also supports CSV file import for bulk operations.
See Image.
To learn more, see Managing a Removable Storage Rule.
# Endpoint Data Scan - End User Report

This feature introduces configurable reports to increase transparency for end users. These reports aim at providing users with best practices and show them where sensitive data is stored locally on their endpoints. This feature aims at making endpoint data scanning more efficient, transparent, and collaborative, improving how administrators and end users work together to manage sensitive data.
To learn more, see Understanding End User Reports, About Endpoint Data Scan, and Analyzing Endpoint DLP Scan for a User.
# Endpoint DLP Configurations
This release introduces the following expanded configuration options across Endpoint Data Scan, Classification, and DLP inspection to improve performance, control, and flexibility:
- Endpoint Data Scan
- Granular controls for End User report visibility, scheduling, sensitive data exposure, and custom messages.
- Ability to exclude specific file systems, folders, and entities.
- Classification Settings
- Option to skip files created by high-volume applications (e.g., compilers) during continuous classification, while still enforcing real-time inspection for exfiltration events.
- Ability to disable OCR for Continuous Classification and Print Control.
- Configurable maximum file size and timeout strategies with Allow or Block fallback actions.
- Channel Configuration
- Per-channel application exclusions for Printer, Clipboard, Removable Storage, and Network Share inspection.
- Option to disable Microsoft Office printing add-ins (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), limiting inspection to print spooler content when disabled.
- Improved removable storage accuracy by ignoring vendor-specific local drives misidentified as removable devices.
- Other Enhancements
- Option to hide the Protect action for end users.
- Controls for Application Inventory Scan.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Endpoint Data Scan and Endpoint Settings and Activating Device Control Policy Rules and Configuration Changes.
# Applications Inventory

The Zscaler Applications page (Analytics > Endpoint Data Scan > Inventory > Applications) provides insights into executable files and applications stored on endpoints, gathering data on installed software, running processes, and libraries. This is crucial not only for compliance, but also for monitoring, auditing, and identifying vulnerabilities or unauthorized software.
See image.
To learn more, see About Inventory and Analyzing Application Details.
# Device Investigation

The Zscaler Device Investigation page (Analytics > Endpoint Data Scan > Device Investigation) provides a comprehensive view of all the endpoint details, including real-time device health status. You can view all the detected applications and the sensitive files stored on the endpoint.
See image.
To learn more, see About Device Investigation and Analyzing Device Investigation Details.
# Sensitive Information Index Document Match (IDM)
To access this feature, contact your Zscaler Account team.

This new capability allows for the detection of data exfiltration on Endpoint DLP channels by matching full or partial content against indexed documents. A secure, endpoint-based workflow has been introduced in this release, enabling authorized users to index sensitive documents directly from their endpoints using the Endpoint DLP context menu. The Endpoint IDM operates in parallel to the Inline DLP IDM. Enforcement and detection are independent and require reindexing of IDM files using the Endpoint DLP. This feature is currently in limited availability. You can access the Sensitive Information page from Analytics > Endpoint Data Scan > Sensitive Information.
See image.
To learn more, see About Sensitive Information and Configuring Sensitive Information Settings.
# Additional Support for Predefined DLP Dictionaries in Endpoint DLP
The following predefined Data Loss Prevention (DLP) dictionaries are supported for use in Endpoint DLP policy rules:
- CNPJ Number (Brazil)
- International Bank Account Number (IBAN)
- National Economic Registry Number (Poland)
- Passport Number (Asia)
To learn more, see Understanding Predefined DLP Dictionaries.
# Added Context for Endpoint DLP Triggers

You can see an additional 15-byte prefix and suffix to the left and right of the Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) trigger that provides more information about the Endpoint DLP incident. The additional context can be seen in the Incident Receiver, Zscaler Workflow Automation, and Email Notifications.
The following image shows an example of trigger context in Zscaler Workflow Automation:

To learn more, see Configuring DLP Notification Templates, Configuring the Zscaler Incident Receiver for On-Premises VMs, Configuring the Zscaler Incident Receiver for Amazon Web Services EC2 VMs, and Configuring the Zscaler Incident Receiver for Azure VMs.
# Endpoint DLP Support for Proximity Length in Predefined Dictionaries

The Zscaler service supports the Proximity Length field on applicable predefined Data Loss Prevention (DLP) dictionaries when used in engines associated with Endpoint DLP rules. The proximity length defines how close a high confidence phrase must be to an instance of the pattern (that the dictionary detects) to count as a match. For certain predefined DLP dictionaries, the Proximity Length field appears when the dictionary’s Confidence Score Threshold is High.
See Image.
To learn more, see Understanding Predefined DLP Dictionaries.

entries.title: Support for New SSPM Controls for GitHub
body: The number of SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) controls for GitHub in Advanced SSPM has been increased. Eleven new SSPM controls are supported for GitHub.

entries.title: Traffic Capture for NDR
body: The Zscaler service can capture traffic in multiple ways:
- Traffic Capture Essentials: Capture traffic as PCAP files with supported actions in ZIA policies when traffic matches policy criteria.
- Traffic Capture for Network Detection and Response (NDR): Capture traffic as PCAPNG files based on criteria specified by the Traffic Capture policy.

Traffic Capture for NDR introduces a standalone Traffic Capture policy page (Policy > Traffic Capture) that enables granular control of Traffic Capture triggers, sampling, and how much traffic is collected per captured connection.
See image.
Information in Traffic Capture for NDR data can be obfuscated on the Traffic Capture Settings page (Administration > Traffic Capture).
See image.
To access Traffic Capture Essentials and Traffic Capture for NDR, contact your Zscaler Account team.

All Zscaler Traffic Capture methods are enabled and disabled on the Traffic Capture Settings page (Administration > Traffic Capture). Connection to your organization's Amazon S3 bucket is also configured on the Traffic Capture Settings page. To learn more, see About Traffic Capture Settings.
To learn more about the Traffic Capture policy, see About Traffic Capture Policy.
# Update to Cloud Service API

The cloud service API includes the following new endpoints to create, update, and delete Traffic Capture policy rules as well as retrieve information for all or specific rules. In addition, they allow you to retrieve the rule count, rule order information, and rule label associations.
- GET /trafficCaptureRules
- POST /trafficCaptureRules
- GET /trafficCaptureRules/{ruleId}
- PUT /trafficCaptureRules/{ruleId}
- DELETE /trafficCaptureRules/{ruleId}
- GET /trafficCaptureRules/count
- GET /trafficCaptureRules/order
- GET /trafficCaptureRules/ruleLabels
To learn more, see the API Reference.

entries.title: Web EUN for DNS Control Policy
body: The DNS Control policy includes an option to display a notification to end users when the policy blocks access to specific domains. Zscaler hosts this End User Notification (EUN) page, eliminating the need for organizations to host their own EUN web page. The DNS EUN web page informs users of the reason for blocking access to specific domains per your organization's security policy. You can customize the notification to display your organization's name, logo, and a custom message.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring the DNS Control Policy, DNS End User Notifications, and Understanding Browser-Based End User Notifications.

entries.title: Apply MIP Label as Manual Remediation Action in SaaS Security Assets
body: For file sharing applications OneDrive and SharePoint, you can apply the MIP label as a manual remediation action from the SaaS Security Assets with Incidents page (Analytics > SaaS Security > Assets > click an application or tenant).
See image.
To learn more, see Understanding the Assets Report: Assets with Incidents and Understanding SaaS Security API Supported Capabilities.

entries.title: Additional Logging of Users Performing Actions on File
body: You can identify and report not only the owner of the file, but also the user who last modified or shared a file that caused a DLP violation, in the ZIA Admin Portal. As part of this feature, the following enhancements are available for Insights Logs and NSS Feeds:
# Insights Logs
The following filters and columns are available on the SaaS Security Insights and SaaS Assets With Incidents page:
- Filters: Last Modified User and Last Shared User
- Columns: Last Modified User, Last Shared User, and Last Shared On
See image.
To learn more, see About the SaaS Security Insights Logs Page and Understanding the Assets Report: Assets with Incidents.
# NSS Feeds

You can add the following fields to the SaaS Security logs Feed Output Format when configuring NSS or Cloud NSS feeds for file applications. These fields provide information on the user who last modified the file, shared the file, and the timestamp when the file was shared, which triggered DLP violations:
- %s{last_edit_user}
- %s{last_share_user}
- %s{last_shared_on}
To learn more, see NSS Feed Output Format: SaaS Security Logs.

entries.title: Create VM Instance using the Virtual Service Edge Azure Terraform Modules
body: You can create a virtual machine (VM) in Azure using the Virtual Service Edge Terraform modules.
To learn more, see Configuring Virtual Service Edge for Microsoft Azure.

entries.title: Enhancement to Custom Views in 3rd-Party App Governance
body: When creating and saving a custom view in 3rd-Party App Governance, you can update the saved view to include your current tenant selection on the global platform filters.
See image.
To learn more, see Custom Views.

entries.title: Creative Commons Search Results
body: Zscaler supports Creative Commons (CC) search for certain search engines (i.e., Bing, Google, and Yahoo). This allows you to see only search results that are licensed under CC. The Enable Creative Commons Search Results option is added to the Policy > URL & Cloud App Control > Advanced Policy Settings page as part of this feature.
This option is disabled by default.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Advanced Policy Settings.

entries.title: Zscaler Client Connector EUNs for Firewall, DNS, and IPS Policies
body: Beginning with Zscaler Client Connector version 4.8 for Windows, ZIA Firewall policies—including Firewall Filtering, DNS Control, and IPS Control—support end user notifications (EUNs) via Zscaler Client Connector. When configuring these policy rules, you can select to show a notification to users and select the notification message that must appear when the rule is triggered. This feature is available on Windows devices running Zscaler Client Connector version 4.8 or later over Z-Tunnel 2.0.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring the Firewall Filtering Policy, Configuring the DNS Control Policy, and Configuring the IPS Control Policy.

You can customize the EUNs for these policy rules under Administration > End User Notifications > Client Connector. You can modify the default notification message and additionally create custom messages to allow the selection of different notification messages for individual policy rules.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring EUNs for Firewall Filtering, Configuring EUNs for DNS Control, Configuring EUNs for IPS Control.

entries.title: Support for Sublocation Scopes
body: You can define scope types and values to map the workload traffic to a sublocation. Defining scopes allows you to apply granular ZIA and Cloud Connector security policies to the workload traffic from that sublocation. You can configure scopes only for Workload traffic type sublocations whose parent locations are associated with Amazon Web Services (AWS) Cloud Connector groups.
As part of this feature, the following fields are added to the Administration > Location Management > Locations > Add Sublocation window:
- Scope
- Account
- Namespace
- VPC
- VPC Endpoint
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing Sublocations, Configuring Sublocations, and Using Sublocation Scopes to Group Cloud Connector Workloads
# Update to Cloud Service API
The Location and LocationLite models used in /locations endpoints within the cloud service API include the following new attributes to support these functionalities via API:
- subLocScopeEnabled
- subLocScope
- subLocScopeValues
- subLocAccIds
To learn more, see the API Reference.

entries.title: JWT Authentication
body: JSON Web Token (JWT) authentication is available for Zscaler Cloud & Branch Connector workloads. JWT authentication is enabled when configuring locations.
See image.
JWT authentication is not supported for the Extranet and IoT Traffic location types.
You can configure JWT authentication exemptions on the Advanced Settings page.
See image.
Token validators for JWT authentication are configured in the Authentication Service Admin Portal.
To learn more, see Understanding JWT Authentication.

entries.title: JWT Authentication Support for Workloads on Management Portal for Partners
body: The ZIA Admin Portal supports a new method, JWT authentication, to authenticate workloads from Cloud & Branch Connector.

In the Management Portal for Partners, you can enable this feature in ZIA for your tenants by using the JWT Auth for Workload field on the Tenant Details page (Tenant > Tenant Details page > Special Settings). To enable this for your tenants, contact the Zscaler Support team.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing Tenant Details.

entries.title: Support for Enhanced US Driver's License Dictionary and Sub-Dictionaries
body: The Zscaler service supports the Enhanced Driver's License (United States) predefined Data Loss Prevention (DLP) dictionary. The parent dictionary contains predefined sub-dictionaries for all 50 U.S. states, plus the District of Columbia, and each sub-dictionary can be individually referenced in your DLP engines.
On the DLP Dictionaries & Engines page (Administration > DLP Dictionaries & Engines), you can expand the Enhanced Driver's License (United States) to see each of the state sub-dictionaries.
See image.
You can then configure each of the individual state sub-dictionaries to set the Confidence Score Threshold, Proximity Length, and any Custom High Confidence Phrases.
See image.
- The Enhanced Driver's License (United States) dictionary is not supported for Endpoint DLP.
- The legacy Driver's License (United States) dictionary has been replaced, but not deprecated, by the Enhanced Driver's License (United States) predefined dictionary.
To learn more, see Understanding Predefined DLP Dictionaries.

entries.title: Updates to SaaS Security Endpoints
body: You can retrieve the SaaS Security Scan Configuration information and the validation status of a SaaS application tenant using the following endpoints:
- GET /casbTenant/scanInfo
- GET /casbTenant/validate/status/{tenantId}
To learn more about each endpoint, see the API Reference and API Rate Limit Summary.
The Postman collection is also updated to include new and updated resources.
To learn more, see Configuring the Postman REST API Client.

entries.title: Automatic Session Restore for Isolation
body: Isolated sessions now automatically restore their web pages if they time out on a user's device. If a session is idle for longer than the timeout of 10 minutes, the isolated page automatically refreshes itself, and the user does not have to sign in again. When this action occurs, the banner notification announcing the start of isolation is disabled. This feature is different than Persistent State, which is enabled per isolation profile to carry over data from an expired session to a new session.
To learn more, see Using Persistent State for Isolation.

entries.title: Original URL of Website Name in Isolation
body: The UI is updated so that when users enter an isolated session, they now see the original URL of the website they are on instead of the isolation web page URL. This change provides users with an experience with a look and feel more like a native browser compared to the container view of being isolated.
To learn more, see User Experience Modes in Isolation.

entries.title: New AI/ML Cloud Applications
body: New cloud applications are added to the cloud application categories. You can download the list of newly added cloud applications to the respective categories: Download
The risk index and risk attribute values for these new applications are visible only after they are available on all the clouds.

entries.title: Document Classification and Logging
body: AI or machine language classification is extended to support around 200 new document types across 10 common document categories.

As part of this extended support, Insights Logs and the Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) are enhanced to provide enriched auto-classification of documents that are uploaded or downloaded during transactions.
The following enhancements are available in the ZIA Admin Portal:
# Updates to Insights Logs

A new filter and column, Subdocument Type, is added to the Web Insights Logs and SaaS Security Insights Logs pages to capture, categorize, and log document subtypes related to administrative documents, invoices, expense reports, and more.
See image.
To learn more, see Web Insights Logs: Filters, Web Insights Logs: Columns, and About SaaS Security Insights Logs.
# Updates to NSS Feeds

The field %s{upload_doc_sub_type} can be added to the Feed Output Format when configuring an NSS or Cloud NSS feed for web logs. Additionally, the field %s{upload_doc_subtype} is available for SaaS Security feeds configured for file applications (e.g., Box). Both fields log the subtype (e.g., Financial Statements: Income Statements (Profit and Loss Statements)) of uploaded or downloaded documents.
To learn more, see NSS Feed Output Format: Web Logs​​​​​​ and NSS Feed Output Format: SaaS Security Logs.

entries.title: Enhancement to SafeSearch
body: SafeSearch allows granular control of applications. This allows you to apply SafeSearch to specific applications. As part of this change, on the Advanced Policy Settings page (Policies > URL & Cloud App Control > Advanced Policy Settings), the SafeSearch Applications drop-down appears when you enable the Enforce SafeSearch option, which lists applications.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Advanced Policy Settings.
# Enhancement to the URL & Cloud App Control Policy Settings Endpoint
A new field safeSearchApps is available for the AdvancedUrlFilteringCloudAppOptions model, referenced in the /advancedUrlFilterAndCloudAppSettings endpoint.
To learn more, go to AdvancedUrlFilteringCloudAppOptions from URL & Cloud App Control Policy Settings.

entries.title: File Type Support for File Type Control & DLP
body: The File Type Control and Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies support the following file types in the Other category:
- UTF-8 BOM
- UTF-16 LE
- UTF-16 BE
The file types are available when creating the following policies:
- File Type Control
- DLP (Rule without content inspection)
To learn more, see About File Type Control and About Data Loss Prevention.

entries.title: New Network Applications in Firewall Control
body: Zscaler includes support for identifying several new network applications using deep packet inspection and controlling the network application traffic using Firewall Filtering rules. These network applications are listed on the Network Applications page (Administration > Network Applications) and are available to be configured in Firewall Filtering rules (Policy > Firewall Control > Firewall Filtering Policy).
List of New Network Applications
- Signal
- HTTP/3
- Proton VPN
- ngrok
- Discord
- Ammyy Admin
- libp2p
- Foureverproxy (4everproxy)
- AnchorFree
- Evasive Protocol
- iTop VPN
- SoftEther VPN
- Wire VPN
To learn more, see About Network Applications and Configuring the Firewall Filtering Policy.

entries.title: Shadow IT Report Enhancements
body: You can view information about the number of transactions per application based on their status (blocked or allowed) in the Cloud Applications table of the Shadow IT Report.
A new column, No. of Transactions, is added to the Cloud Applications table.
See image.
To learn more, see About the Shadow IT Report.

entries.title: Support for Custom File Types in DLP and File Type Control Policies
body: You can create custom file types and use them when creating Data Loss Prevention (DLP) and File Type Control policies. You can then filter and view logs for these custom file types in Web Insights Logs and the Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS).
See image.
As part of this enhancement, the Download User-Defined File Type and Upload User-Defined File Type filters and columns are added to the Web Insights Logs.
See Image.
To learn more, see:
- Configuring Custom File Types
- Configuring the File Type Control Policy
- Configuring DLP Policy Rules with Evaluate All Rules Mode Enabled
- Configuring DLP Policy Rules with Content Inspection
- Configuring DLP Policy Rules without Content Inspection
- Web Insights Logs: Columns
- Web Insights Logs: Filters

Additionally, filters for Download User-Defined File Type and Upload User-Defined File Type are added to NSS and Cloud NSS feeds for web logs as well as Microsoft Cloud App Security (MCAS) NSS feeds. You can use these filters to limit the logs sent to your security information and event management (SIEM) system based on the custom type of files that were downloaded or uploaded during the transaction.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding NSS Feeds for Web Logs, Adding Cloud NSS Feeds for Web Logs, and Adding MCAS NSS Feeds.
# Update to Cloud Service API

The cloud service API includes the following new endpoints to create, update, and delete custom file types, retrieve information about custom file types and the count of custom file types, and retrieve information about all file types that can be used as rule conditions in DLP and File Type Control policies.
- GET /fileTypeCategories
- GET /customFileTypes
- POST /customFileTypes
- PUT /customFileTypes
- GET /customFileTypes/{id}
- DELETE /customFileTypes/{id}
- GET /customFileTypes/count

In addition, the fileTypes attribute used in /webDlpRules and /fileTypeRules endpoints is replaced with a new fileTypeCategories attribute to specify both predefined and custom file types along with their ID, name, and parent file category. Zscaler recommends updating your API configurations to use the new attribute. The ZmanageNssFeed model used in the /nssFeeds endpoints additionally includes two new attributes, namely customDownloadFiletype and customUploadFiletype, to filter logs based on the custom file types downloaded and uploaded during the transaction, respectively.
To learn more, see the API Reference.

entries.title: Support for Custom File Types in File Type Policies and DLP
body: The File Type Control and Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies now support custom file types with extension-based detection.

On the Management Portal for Partners, partner tenants can see a new field, Custom File Type Limit, in their Technical Information section. The Custom File Type Limit indicates the number of custom file types that can be created for File Type Control and DLP policies in the ZIA Admin Portal.
See image.
To learn more, see About File Type Control, Configuring the File Type Control Policy, and Viewing Tenant Details.

entries.title: Support for Quarantine File to Desired Location
body: The SaaS Security Data at Rest Scanning DLP and Malware policies support specifying the location to quarantine files for the file sharing applications Google Drive, Microsoft OneDrive, and Microsoft SharePoint.
# SaaS Application Tenant Onboarding

Onboarding a SaaS application tenant with Data at Rest Scanning DLP and Malware policies includes the functionality to specify your quarantine location for policy violating files. Provide a quarantine location and a DLP admin mail ID while onboarding the SaaS tenant. Also note, the DLP admin should have read/write access to the quarantine folder path.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding SaaS Application Tenants.
# Quarantine Files That Violate DLP Policy in a Desired Location
On the SaaS Security Data at Rest Scanning Edit DLP / Malware policy page, select the Admin Quarantine action to isolate sensitive files in the location of your choice.
See image.

To learn more, see About Data at Rest Scanning DLP, Configuring the Data at Rest Scanning DLP Policy with Content Inspection, and Configuring the Data at Rest Scanning DLP Policy without Content Inspection.
# Remediation Actions in Assets with Incidents Page

The following options are added as part of remediation actions for file sharing applications Google Drive, Microsoft OneDrive, and Microsoft SharePoint on the Assets with Incidents page (Analytics > SaaS Security > Assets > Assets with Incidents):
- Admin Quarantine: To quarantine sensitive files to a specific file location
- Restore Admin Quarantine: To restore a file that was previously quarantined to the admin-specified location.
See image.
To learn more, see Understanding the Assets Report: Assets with Incidents and Understanding SaaS Security API Supported Capabilities.

entries.title: Support for Adaptive Access Engine
body: Adaptive Access Engine dynamically manages access based on real-time assessments of risk and trust by continuously evaluating contextual signals, user behavior, device health, location, and other factors to determine whether to allow or block access to websites or apps at any given moment. You can configure URL Filtering and Cloud App Control policies using adaptive access profiles.
See image.

This feature is currently not functional in the ZIA Admin Portal and is only supported in Experience Center under Limited Availability. To subscribe to Experience Center, contact your Zscaler Account team.
To learn more, see Adding Rules to the Cloud App Control Policy and Configuring the URL Filtering Policy.
# Logs for Adaptive Access Profile
As part of this update, a filter and column, Adaptive Access Profile, is added to Web Insights Logs.
See image.
To learn more, see Web Insights Logs: Columns and Web Insights Logs: Filters.

entries.title: Support for New SSPM Controls for Snowflake
body: The number of SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) controls for Snowflake in Advanced SSPM has been increased. Forty-six new SSPM controls are supported for Snowflake.

entries.title: Logs for Post-Quantum Cryptography Visibility
body: Zscaler is proactively preparing for post-quantum cryptography (PQC) by evaluating quantum-safe algorithms, supporting hybrid encryption systems, and enabling scalable integration of quantum-resilient technologies across its cloud infrastructure. Zscaler collaborates globally with standardization bodies like NIST, provides customers with enablement tools, and ensures its platform is future-proofed for crypto-agility, facilitating a seamless transition to secure PQC solutions.

Enhancements to Insights Logs and the Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) provide visibility into the PQC capabilities of TLS client- and server-side connections. You can filter and view ZIA web logs based on key exchange and digital signature algorithms.
As part of the update, the following changes are available in the ZIA Admin Portal:
# Interactive Reports: Post-Quantum Cryptography Visibility

The Post-Quantum Cryptography Visibility Report (Analytics > Interactive Reports > Web Activity) provides insights into the most frequently used PQC Key Algorithms and SSL/TLS versions. It also displays the distribution of transactions, differentiating between traffic processed with PQC and non-PQC methods. To further investigate the types of PQC methods used, you can drill down to the Web Logs.
See image.
To learn more, see About Interactive Reports, Understanding the Post-Quantum Cryptography Visibility Report, and Viewing the Post-Quantum Cryptography Visibility Report.
# Web Insights Data Types
The following data types are added to Web Insights:
- PQC vs. Classical Key Exchange
- Top PQC Key Exchange Algorithms
- Top Users with PQC Key Exchange
See image.
To learn more, see Web Data Types and Filters.
# Web Insights Logs
The following filters and columns are added to Web Insights Logs:
- Client Digital Signature Proposal
- Client Key Exchange Proposal
- Client-Side Key Exchange Algorithm
- Server-Side Key Exchange Algorithm
- Client-Side Digital Signature Algorithm
- Server-Side Digital Signature Algorithm
See image.
To learn more, see Web Insights Logs: Columns and Web Insights Logs: Filters.
# NSS Feeds for Web Logs
